global_decisions.decision: Single NestJS package rooted at backend/ (backend/package.json, pnpm). TypeScript path aliases give module boundaries: @carpal/libs/*, @carpal/modules/*, @carpal/workers/*. Nest CLI monorepo mode with apps under backend/apps/{api,admin-api,auth,worker}.
global_decisions.reason: One deployable codebase (41 §1). A single package avoids workspace overhead while there is no frontend consumer. dependency-cruiser enforces the boundaries instead of package borders. A repo-level pnpm workspace can be added when shared/ gets consumers.

amendments.change: The package is ESM ("type": "module") because NestJS 12 ships ESM only. Module aliases are package.json subpath imports (#apps/*, #libs/*, #modules/*, #workers/*, #tools/*) with a "source" condition (TS sources for tsc/tsx/Vitest, dist/ for node), not TS path aliases. No nest-cli: `pnpm build` = tsc -p tsconfig.build.json + tools/copy-build-assets.mjs (copies generated JSON).

global_decisions.decision: SQL-first data access: Kysely + pg. DB types are generated from the live schema with kysely-codegen. No ORM, and no ORM-managed migrations.
global_decisions.reason: The schema, RLS, triggers and seeds already exist as SQL (43), and every transaction must call core.set_context(). A query builder keeps SQL visible and type-safe.

global_decisions.decision: Request/response validation uses ajv (JSON Schema 2020-12, closed objects). Schemas are generated from the doc-40 type notation where the parser can handle it. Types it cannot handle get hand-written schemas in the owning module's api/ folder.
global_decisions.reason: 40 §0.1 says its notation maps 1:1 to JSON Schema 2020-12, and OpenAPI 3.1 uses the same dialect.

global_decisions.decision: Infrastructure goes behind ports, with two adapter sets chosen by CARPAL_INFRA=lite|full. Lite: embedded PostgreSQL (see S1.T3), in-memory key-value store, in-process event bus and job queue, in-memory search index, local-filesystem object storage under backend/.data/, file/log sinks for email/SMS/push. Full: PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector, Redis, NATS JetStream, BullMQ, Elasticsearch, S3/MinIO, Mailpit, via infrastructure/docker/docker-compose.yml.
global_decisions.reason: No Docker or servers on this machine. Business code depends only on the ports, so full mode needs no code changes.

amendments.change: Lite DB runtime chosen: embedded-postgres 16.14.0-beta.17 (real PostgreSQL 16, real login roles and RLS, concurrent connections). PGlite was not needed. The cluster is run with pg_ctl so it survives the CLI process (data: backend/.data/pg, port 54329, 127.0.0.1 only, fsync off).

Lite adapters are per process (in-memory KV, bus, queue; files under .data/), so pnpm dev runs api, admin-api, auth and the worker in one process. Full-mode adapters exist as typed skeletons that reject with NotConfiguredError.

ObjectStorage.put takes { encrypt }: lite stores such objects AES-256-GCM (key derived from the master secret, AAD = object key) and decrypts on read and serve; full mode maps it to SSE-KMS. Geocoder is a port bound by PlatformModule (lite FixtureGeocoder, full UnconfiguredGeocoder → 503). sharp (prebuilt) is the image codec of W6 in both modes.

SearchIndex port redesigned (libs/infra/ports.ts): typed filters (eq/in/all/range/exists/not/any on dotted paths), analyzed text with field boosts (all/any, prefix and one-edit typo matches), geo radius with a per-point service radius and bbox, removeWhere, get and ids. Lite: MemorySearchIndex (per process, text analyzed by libs/i18n searchTokens). Full: OpenSearchIndex written to the same port (REST via fetch, analyzed tokens stored per field) but unverified (OQ-01). EmailMessage/SmsMessage gained rendered subject/text; PushMessage gained platform and the decrypted token (the lite sink drops the token).

global_decisions.decision: The router registers all 402 operations from the generated registry from day one. An operation without a handler returns 501 with problem code NOT_IMPLEMENTED. This is a dev-only deviation from 40 §4.3, and it must be zero (or explicitly listed) by the end of S9.
global_decisions.reason: Fail-closed routing (40 'no undocumented endpoints') from the start, plus a measurable coverage number per stage.

amendments.change: The 501 is answered after authentication, rate limits, authorization and feature flags and before input validation, so unimplemented routes still prove their guards. Problem code NOT_IMPLEMENTED (outside the 40 catalog). After S2: 398 operations answer 501.

After S3: 59 operations implemented, 343 answer 501. Test-only handlers (apps/testing handlerModule) are marked as overrides (markOverride) and replace the real handler of the same operation, so pipeline tests keep exercising real op ids; two real handlers for one operation still fail at startup.
After S4: 130 operations implemented, 272 answer 501 (3 deferred S3 ops). media.upload_put is served by the storage listener, not the API router.
After S5: 191 operations implemented, 211 answer 501 (3 of them the deferred S3 operations). vehicle 31/31, inventory 30/32 (the 2 others are the §14.3 public reads of S6).

After S6: 236 operations implemented, 166 answer 501 (3 of them the deferred S3 operations). discovery 7/7, community 25/25, notification 7/7, inventory 32/32, organization 64/71, trust 1/36, appointment 1/31.
After S7: 293 operations implemented, 109 answer 501 (3 of them the deferred S3 operations). appointment 31/31, trust 28/36 (the other 8 are §23.4 admin operations of S8).

After S8: 375 operations implemented, 27 answer 501 (23 §21 AI operations, 3 deferred S3 identity operations, media.upload_put = storage PUT). fleet 20/20, admin 16/16, analytics 3/3, identity 58/61, organization 71/71, billing 7/7, taxonomy 13/13, trust 36/36, media 10/11, ai-mcp 4/27; admin-api serves 60/60 routes.

global_decisions.decision: Scratch auth: real EdDSA JWTs, server-side sessions with refresh rotation and family revocation, Argon2id passwords, TOTP. DPoP, mTLS, app attestation, PoW and WebAuthn are coded as guard hooks and enforced only when CARPAL_STRICT_AUTH=1. Until then they are logged deviations.
global_decisions.reason: Keeps the security model in place without blocking feature stages on the hardest protocol work.

amendments.change: Strict-mode hooks implemented: DPoP proof verification is complete (ES256 embedded key, htm/htu/iat/ath/jkt, jti replay in the KV store; server nonces left to S3), mTLS compares cnf x5t#S256 with the thumbprint supplied by the TLS terminator, ATT calls an AttestationVerifierPort (S3). The admin plane requires aal3 staff sessions in both modes.

Auth server implemented: authorization code + PKCE S256 through a cookie-bound hosted sign-in interaction (__Host-cp_ia), refresh-token rotation where a token family = one server-side session (reuse revokes the session and mails a security alert), client credentials (cp-ssr, public.read), the anonymous grant (15 min, public.read search), ID tokens (EdDSA, nonce), revocation. DPoP proofs are verified at /oauth/token and bind tokens (cnf.jkt, token_type DPoP); strict mode requires a proof from cp-mobile and a server nonce (400 use_dpop_nonce + DPoP-Nonce). The ATT verifier accepts proof-of-work solutions of auth.pow_challenge (single use); platform attestation tokens are refused. Still not implemented (logged deviations): WebAuthn (passkeys, staff aal3 sign-in), Google/Apple sign-in, App Attest / Play Integrity verification, private_key_jwt / mTLS client authentication for the BFF clients, DPoP-Nonce on the API hosts, risk-based sign-in (SEC-AU-12).

global_decisions.decision: AI is never called directly. The ai-mcp facade module talks to an McpClientPort. In lite mode the port is a deterministic stub that returns schema-valid drafts, or 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE when the flag or kill switch says so. The real MCP gateway and orchestrator (ai-mcp/ folder, D6/D7) are out of scope for this backend build.
global_decisions.reason: 41 §1 rule 4 and 40 SEC-AI. The user asked for the backend; ai-mcp/ is a separate deployable.

global_decisions.decision: Tests: Jest (with @swc/jest) + supertest. Integration tests run against the real embedded PostgreSQL with RLS on, connecting as the real application roles (carpal_api, carpal_admin_api, carpal_worker, carpal_auth), never as superuser.
global_decisions.reason: 41 §8. RLS is the second wall of tenancy (40 SEC-AZ-3) and only real role connections test it.

amendments.change: Vitest 5 instead of Jest (41 §8 names Jest): Jest ESM support is still experimental and the package is ESM. unplugin-swc compiles TS so decorator metadata is emitted. Projects: unit (*.test.ts) and integration (*.int.test.ts, global setup starts the DB and runs db:setup).

global_decisions.decision: The database migrations are generated from Docs/43.db_setup.sql by a build script into database/migrations/. Generated files are never edited by hand: fix 43 (and 42) and regenerate. Changes after the first install become numbered migrations (0100+), written by hand.
global_decisions.reason: 42 §1: the script is authoritative and later changes are numbered migrations.

amendments.change: No generated split migration files. Docs/43.db_setup.sql is run as-is by a psql-compatible runner (tools/db/psql: \set, \if/\elif/\else/\endif, \gset, \gexec, \connect, \echo, :var/:'var'/:"var"/:{?var}); its SHA-256 is stored in core.schema_info (baseline.sha256). database/migrations/NNNN_*.sql run afterwards as carpal_migrator + SET ROLE carpal_owner. Real psql works too (full mode).

global_decisions.decision: Project-local Node 24 LTS (backend/.node-version = 24.21.0) under backend/.tools/node; engines ">=22.12". Current tool majors are used (TypeScript 5.9, Vitest 5, ESLint 10, dependency-cruiser 18).
global_decisions.reason: The user keeps the system Node 20.10 for another project until it ends, then upgrades to Node 24 LTS. Current tooling needs Node >= 22.12.

amendments.change: engines raised to >=24.7: password hashing uses node:crypto argon2 (Argon2id, no native npm dependency). TypeScript target/lib ES2024 (String.isWellFormed).

global_decisions.decision: The contract is generated, never hand-copied: libs/contract/generated/ (operations.json, schemas.json, operation-schemas.json, operation-ids.ts, errors.ts, enums.ts, role-groups.ts, schema-coverage.json) from Docs/40 by tools/contract/generate.ts. CI (S9) runs pnpm contract:check; a unit test fails when the files are stale.
global_decisions.reason: 40 is authoritative and changes; generation keeps the router, validation and tests aligned with it.

amendments.change: Generator fixes (tools/contract/generate.ts), regenerated operation-schemas.json: (1) GET list operations returning Page<T> without a q: line now accept cursor/limit (40 §3.3; 26 ops, e.g. dsr.list, me.mfa_list, onboarding.list; POST searches page in their bodies); (2) non-Id path parameters that 40 leaves untyped (flow_type, slug, report_type, role, key, dashboard_key) get their schema types (DI-12) instead of the Id pattern, which made those routes unreachable; (3) createContractAjv accepts validating replacements of the x- keywords (x-node-type, GD-17).
Docs/40 changed and the contract was regenerated: Problem gained optional requirements, consent_type, entitlement_key (DI-10); OrgMember gained version and nullable user_id/full_name (DI-19, DI-22).

The Vin type carries the annotation keyword x-vin (tools/contract/types/json-schema.ts, regenerated): the validator upper-cases Vin body fields and converts Persian/Arabic digits before the pattern check (40 §3.1 "after uppercasing and digit normalization"), and a body whose only failures are Vin fields is 422 VIN_INVALID (40 §4.4) instead of VALIDATION_FAILED.

global_decisions.decision: HTTP layer: no Nest controllers and no Nest platform adapter. libs/http-pipeline registers the routes of operations.json per host on node:http and runs the 41 §5 steps as explicit code; NestJS (application context) provides dependency injection, modules, lifecycle and DiscoveryService to find @Operation(opId) handlers.
global_decisions.reason: Routes must come only from the contract (SEC-AZ-1) with exact 404/405/501 behaviour, a fixed step order, raw-body access for strict JSON and idempotency hashing, and no framework headers. Decorator-based controllers would duplicate the registry; dynamic Express routes would still need custom ordering and parsing.

amendments.change: POST searches page in their bodies (40 §3.3, TR-7): when the input schema has a cursor member, the pipeline verifies body.cursor like a query cursor and binds it (and ctx.page) to the body filters without cursor and limit (CURSOR_MISMATCH when they change). Used by inventory.search; search.run and the public searches of S6 get it for free.

OperationContext.cursorFor(opId, params, position) signs a cursor for another operation of the same host (bound to that route and path parameters, no query filters): search.run and search.refine answer next_cursor for search.page.

global_decisions.decision: Integration-test database strategy: one shared database per test run (db:setup once), never reset between tests; fixtures (libs/testing) write through carpal_worker in the system context with fresh UUIDv7 ids and @test.carpal.app emails, the app under test connects with its real role, and tests assert only on their own rows.
global_decisions.reason: Template clones lose the per-database role settings (S1 notes); per-test rollback cannot wrap an HTTP app with its own transactions; truncation is blocked on append-only tables. Unique fixtures keep RLS real and tests fast (the 3.5k-request sweep takes about 3 s).

global_decisions.decision: The auth host runs every transaction in the system RLS context. Its database role carpal_auth has identity grants only (plus billing.plans), and all its operations are PUB(no token); the pipeline sets actorType system for the auth host.
global_decisions.reason: 42 §5.1 assigns the system context to carpal_auth; sign-up, sign-in and link consumption act for an account that is not authenticated yet, and AUD operations must write their audit entry through ctx.tx (the pipeline checks the audit mark).

global_decisions.decision: Cross-module extension points live in the owning module's interface/ folder, as abstract-class ports or registries: billing UsageCounters (counter entitlements and Subscription.usage) and SubscriptionReader; identity UserCards, ConsentScopes (scope-ownership checks for consents.grant) and DataExportFiles (DSR download); organization OrgCards; taxonomy TaxonomyResolver. Registries are created with useFactory, so each Nest application context has its own (pnpm dev and the tests run several contexts in one process). Modules register into them in onModuleInit; an unregistered extension fails closed.
global_decisions.reason: Keeps dependency-cruiser module boundaries (no module reads another module's tables) while later stages plug in their data (vehicles, inventory, media, appointments).

amendments.change: New extension points: organization OrganizationExtensions (visits, customer checks, vehicle owners, inventory item counter, insight sources) and media AttachmentTargets (attachable record types with owner + role groups). New interfaces: identity AccountFacts, OrgMemberships, ConsentRequests; billing SubscriptionWriter; organization ProviderCapabilities, PublicProfiles; media MediaService. Unregistered extensions fail closed.

New extension points and interfaces in S5: vehicle VehicleCards (definer cards, visible-vehicle lookup) and VehicleService (recordAppointmentService, markIssueScheduled for S7); inventory InventoryRead (visibleIds, publicCards, publicItem for S6); identity ConsentGrants (a consent created atomically with another module's record, no scope verifier: the inquiry's vendor_fitment_context); organization VendorCatalog (catalog_quality_score and measured_response_time_minutes written by inventory, only when they change), OrgLocations (active location check), PublicProfiles.vendors (published vendors and their trade_customers_supported flag); media MediaService.syncAttachments, imageCounts, assetUrls, publicImageUrls, readContent, storeGenerated, signedDownload. Registered: billing UsageCounters max_vehicles and max_inventory_items; organization visits service_record, customer check, vehicle owners, item counter and four vendor insight sources; media targets vehicle, vehicle_issue, inventory_item; identity ConsentScopes vehicle and stock_inquiry. OrganizationExtensions.VisitInfo gained jobLogVerification: a job log linked to a visit inherits customer_confirmed, appointment_verified or invoice_verified (54 §1.1).

New interfaces: organization PublicOrgCards (full 40 PublicOrgCard with trust figures and the newest public portfolio image) and PublicProfiles.idBySlug/cards/searchSources/publishedIds/changedSince/portfolio/portfolioItems/portfolioSources/portfolioIds/portfolioItemStatus; inventory InventoryRead.searchSources/vendorItemIds/tradeVendorIds; trust TrustRead (ratings, ratingSummary, badges, publishedReviewSubject); community CommunityRead (search sources, public refs, favourites, follows, followers, recent questions and posts); identity Recipients (verified contacts, locale, critical_alerts_only, members by role) and authorDisplayName(); notification Messenger (EN/FA transactional mails); media MediaService.publicAttachmentViews; taxonomy TaxonomyResolver.descendants/catalog; vehicle VehicleCards.openReminders. Registered: media attachment targets post, question, answer (community). New consumers: organization.reaction_changed (portfolio like_count), notification.dispatch (W5), discovery.search_indexer (W2).

New interfaces: appointment AppointmentFacts; organization ProviderBooking and TrustFigures; discovery MatchResults; trust TrustRead.appointmentReviewState (and the exported TrustScorer, Invitations, ReviewWorkflow inside the trust module); vehicle VehicleCards.serviceVisits/serviceHistory/issue/appointmentRecords; inventory InventoryRead.inquiryVisits; media MediaService.sharedAttachmentViews; identity AccountFacts.verifiedEmail and ConsentGrants service_history_sharing. Registered: organization visits appointment (job logs inherit appointment_verified from completed appointments), the appointment customer check, insight sources provider.requests_received/completion_rate (appointment) and provider.overall_rating/review_count/category_ratings (trust); media attachment targets appointment and review; identity ConsentScopes appointment. New consumers: trust.review_workflow (W4), trust.scoring (W3), trust.helpful_count.

New registries (useFactory per context): admin FourEyesExecutors, PurposeQueues, ModerationTargets, RetentionHandlers; identity PersonalDataRegistry; taxonomy TaxonomyReferences; analytics MetricGauges. New ports/interfaces: admin FourEyes, ModerationLog, StaffNames; identity AccountAdmin; trust TrustAdmin; organization OrgLifecycle; fleet FleetDrivers, FleetWorkflow, FleetPartners (and libs/authz DriverAssignments bound); billing staff summaries; vehicle fleet reads and createFleetVehicle; appointment fleetAppointments; media moderateAttached. Every module registers its admin parts in application/admin-registrations.ts.

global_decisions.decision: Taxonomy is served from an in-memory catalog in every process (all nodes, active synonyms and mappings; about 1,700 rows). A fingerprint (row counts + newest updated_at of the three tables) is re-checked at most every CARPAL_TAXONOMY_REFRESH_MS (30 s); a change reloads the catalog, and taxonomy.node.merged drops it at once (each process subscribes to the bus with its own consumer name). The taxonomy version is derived from the fingerprint ("t<base36 ms>-<base36 rows>") and is also what config.client reports.
global_decisions.reason: 41 §2.1 M4 ("served and cached for every other module"); the vocabulary is small and public, typeahead and NodeId checks must not hit the database, and the version must change whenever the content does.

global_decisions.decision: NodeId<type> fields of request bodies are enforced by the pipeline: the x-node-type keyword collects (pointer, id, allowed types) during closed-schema validation, and the NodeTypeChecker port (taxonomy module) answers 422 REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND for unknown or inactive nodes and 422 TAXONOMY_MISMATCH for nodes of another type, all problems in one response. A body with node references fails closed (500) on a host without the checker. Parent chains (model under brand, series under model) stay with the use cases (TaxonomyResolver.requireDescendant).
global_decisions.reason: 40 §3.1 NodeId<type> and SEC-AZ-4; S1 left x-node-type as an annotation for S3.

global_decisions.decision: Media pipeline: media.upload_complete marks the asset active/pending and enqueues the asset id on the media.process queue after commit; W6 (MediaProcessor, worker deployable, system context) sniffs, scans, re-encodes and re-stores the processed variants (media/<id>/original|display|thumb; the raw uploads/<id> object is deleted when clean) and publishes media.scan.completed in the same transaction as the status. A W15 rule re-queues assets still pending after CARPAL_MEDIA_RESCAN_AFTER_MS (processing is idempotent), another discards uploads never completed. Redaction runs as a core.background_jobs job (kind redaction, queue media.redaction) whose input_summary carries only relative coordinates.
global_decisions.reason: 41 §2.4 W6 is triggered by media.upload_complete; a queue entry plus a database sweep gives at-least-once processing without an extra event type, and keeps the scan status and its event atomic.

global_decisions.decision: Organization lifecycle in S4: org.create inserts a draft organization (RLS create_draft) with the creator's owner membership and the audience's default plan in one transaction; the first successful provider.publish or vendor.publish moves a draft organization to active (DI-18). Fleets stay draft until S8 decides their activation (fleet profile).
global_decisions.reason: 52 §21 requires an active organization to publish but no operation of 40 activates one, and 56 §2.11 allows publishing while verification is pending.

amendments.change: Decided: a draft (or pending_verification) fleet organization becomes active with its first fleet.profile_put, through organization OrgLifecycle.activate (authz cache refreshed after commit).

global_decisions.decision: DRV in a principal alternative admits fleet drivers in addition to the ORG role group (ORG(FC) DRV = FC + fleet_driver), always limited to vehicles assigned to them: on routes with a path vehicle the authorizer checks DriverAssignments per request (also for a qualified DRV such as DRV(own reports), whose qualifier the use case applies on top); lists are filtered by the use case (grant.driverScoped). A driver admitted only through DRV gets matchedGroups ["DRV"]. The BOLA/BFLA matrix (libs/testing) follows the same rule.
global_decisions.reason: 40 issues.create (ORG(FC) DRV) says a fleet driver's report starts the fleet approval workflow, and mileage_add is ORG(FC) DRV, but FC does not contain fleet_driver: read as an AND, drivers could never report. 40 §0.4 defines DRV as "fleet driver: allowed only on vehicles with an active FleetVehicleAssignment". Until S8 binds real assignments (NoDriverAssignments), drivers reach no vehicle (fail closed).

amendments.change: Assignments are real: DbDriverAssignments (fleet) answers the authorizer in the driver's own RLS context (the API roles cannot use the system context); vehicles.list filters drivers set-based (FleetDrivers.assignedVehicleIds); appointments list/get show drivers their own requests and those of assigned vehicles.

global_decisions.decision: W7 import-jobs (workers/import-jobs): CSV files are parsed by libs/csv (strict RFC 4180, UTF-8, the SEC-IN-11 limits, no evaluation; a formula-safe writer for error reports and exports). Rows are mapped by ImportCreate.column_mapping onto InventoryItemWrite fields (name_translations.<locale>, lists split on | or ;), normalized like API input (SEC-IN-4), validated with the contract input schemas of inventory.create / inventory.update (ContractValidator) and the module rules, and upserted by SKU in transactions of 200 rows with one SAVEPOINT per row, so a bad row never loses its chunk. Row errors become a private system_export media asset of the vendor (line, field, code, then the row as uploaded). Durable job input lives in core.background_jobs.input_summary (batch id; item ids and patch for bulk updates: no personal data), so a lost queue entry can be re-run. A job that only changes existing records (bulk_inventory_update) succeeds without a result (Docs/43 check relaxed, JobOutcome { result: null }).
global_decisions.reason: 40 inventory.import_create / bulk_update are ASYNC (202 Job) and SEC-IN-11 fixes the dialect and limits; no CSV dependency was needed for a strict dialect. The contract schemas are the single definition of a valid item, so imported rows cannot bypass them; per-row savepoints give "the job succeeds with an error report" (S5 acceptance) without one bad row aborting others.

global_decisions.decision: Community text is pre-moderated automatically (modules/community/domain/rules.ts autoModeration): posts, comments, questions and answers are approved at once unless their text carries a link, an email address or a phone number (also in Persian/Arabic digits), which stays moderation_status pending for the S8 moderation queue. Edits are moderated again; a published post whose edited text is held leaves publication (status draft). Media follow 52 §15 and stay private until moderation approves them (S8).
global_decisions.reason: 40 says community content is "moderated before it becomes visible", the DB public_read policies require moderation_status approved, and the moderation queue is S8; without an automated decision no question, answer, comment or post could ever be seen. Contact data and links are the main spam and off-platform risk. Product to confirm (OQ-12).

global_decisions.decision: Search: five projections (indices providers, vendors, inventory, community, taxonomy; 52 §10) built by SearchProjections (modules/discovery/infrastructure) from the owning modules' interfaces in the worker's system context, written through the SearchIndex port. W2 (discovery.search_indexer consumer, workers/search-indexer) rebuilds what an event touches; a W15 sweep (discovery.search_sweep, every minute) reindexes organizations whose public tables changed (PublicProfiles.changedSince) to cover edits without events; the nightly discovery.search_reconcile rebuilds everything and drops what is no longer public, and its first run at worker start rebuilds the lite in-memory index (CARPAL_SEARCH_REBUILD_ON_START, off in tests). Query interpretation is rule-based: analyzed n-grams looked up in the taxonomy projection (names and synonyms, every locale), target words, stop words and region cities; ranking follows 54 §5 in pure functions (domain/ranking.ts) with structured reasons stored on match_results and rendered per reader locale. Sessions store up to 100 ranked results; cards are rebuilt from current public data on every page.
global_decisions.reason: 41 §2.4 W2 and 52 §10 (projections rebuilt from events, not system of record); the lite index is per process, so a start-up rebuild and a sweep keep it correct without events for every organization table; the same normalization (libs/i18n searchTokens) on documents and queries makes Persian/Arabic variants and digits match.

global_decisions.decision: Notifications (W5): events are routed to intents in a pure table (modules/notification/domain/routing.ts: audience users / organization members by role / followers, event_type, category, priority, template, plain params). The dispatcher writes one Notification per recipient (recipient locale) with its deliveries in one transaction, then sends queued deliveries through the Mailer/PushSender/SmsSender ports and records sent/failed (attempt_count, last_error). Critical notifications skip preferences (always in-app; email and push); otherwise the merged preference decides; email digests wait for notification.digests; business notifications (organization context) go to portal web push tokens only. Retries: notification.delivery_retry (3 attempts). Transactional messages that carry secrets (verification links, codes, invitations, consent links) never become notifications: they go through the Messenger (EN/FA templates) synchronously.
global_decisions.reason: 52 Notification/NotificationDelivery/NotificationPreference rules, 41 §6.2; link tokens and codes must not travel through the outbox or be stored in template_params.

amendments.change: S7 routes (appointments, reviews, invitations, inquiry answers) in routing.ts routeS7; the ci check-in link, review invitation links and their one-time codes are Messenger mails (appointment.check_in_link, review.invitation, review.invitation_code), never notifications.

routeS8: fleet.approval.requested (only with approval_id), fleet.approval.decided, moderation.action.taken (affected user or organization admins), organization.verified, organization.location.corrected, dsr.deadline.approaching (staff); EN/FA templates added.

global_decisions.decision: Appointments: confirmation re-checks capacity in its transaction under a per-location transaction advisory lock (appointment.capacity_available, now SECURITY DEFINER, or time off only for a location without any active availability rule); slots for public.availability and the calendar are computed per request from the rules, time off and the busy_intervals definer (no slot cache); the pre-visit report is generated in the requester's transaction and stored, the provider reading history only while the service_history_sharing consent is granted; parties' contact data reach the other side only through definers bound to the appointment (requester_contact, check_in_contact) and Messenger mails.
global_decisions.reason: 52 §12 ("concurrent bookings cannot exceed capacity"), SEC-AZ-8 and SEC-OUT-3: the provider can never read the customer's vehicle, history or contact data directly, and the requester's context cannot count other parties' appointments. Providers without a calendar must still be able to accept requests in the MVP.

global_decisions.decision: Reviews and trust: the server decides the confirmation path at reviews.create (Path 1 from a visit of the author that took place, inside the 7-day window for appointments; Path 2 otherwise, business-confirmed when a business sent the invitation); W4 publishes Path 1 reviews after text checks; W3 recomputes one organization from scratch on every relevant event and nightly (evidence rows synced through organization TrustFigures — inserted active, revoked, never edited — capability confidence, trust score with penalties, change-only trust signals, rule badges with audit and events, staleness). Scores and weights are the 54 launch defaults under RULE_VERSION 54-2026-10.
global_decisions.reason: 52 §11/§21 and 54: evidence over claims, no unverified reviews, idempotent recomputation converges with at-least-once events and the nightly sweep; the organization module owns capabilities and the trust_score column (GD-15), the trust module owns every number.

global_decisions.decision: Admin plane mechanics: (1) every admin handler lives in the module that owns the operation (registry module), with staffOf(ctx); (2) 4EYES operations file a pending change (FourEyes.request, one pending per op and target, 72 h) and return 202 PendingChange; approval runs the executor the owning module registered (FourEyesExecutors) inside the approver's transaction, then marks the change approved — requester ≠ approver (also the DB check), moderators decide required_role platform_moderator changes only; (3) CarPal-Access-Purpose is verified by the authorizer through PurposeQueues resolvers owned by the module of each queue (case: open and unassigned/assigned to the caller; dispute: idem; dsr, verification, approval: open items of shared queues); (4) staff reads of private data write pii.read with the purpose (auditStaffRead) and the pipeline refuses a staff PII response without an audit entry (dev/test); (5) moderation acts on other modules' records only through ModerationTargets (exists, snapshot, subjectOrganization, author, apply, pending); (6) RSN on DELETE reads CarPal-Reason (DI-09).
global_decisions.reason: 40 §23 / SEC-ADM-3..6 and GD-15: staff need cross-module powers, but every table stays owned by its module; executors and resolvers keep the rules next to the data.

global_decisions.decision: Product analytics: events.ingest validates client events against a registry (names, property kinds, ±skew) and enqueues accepted batches (analytics.ingest); the worker pseudonymizes actors with analytics.actor_pseudonyms (HMAC-SHA256 of the user id under a per-user key; no key is created for deleted accounts) and writes events.analytics_events in carpal_analytics as carpal_analytics_writer; business events are copied by the analytics.pipeline consumer with allowlisted non-personal payload keys. Daily metrics: hourly recomputation of yesterday and today (event counts per name, gauges registered by owning modules) read with carpal_analytics_reader; dashboards read daily_metrics only.
global_decisions.reason: 52 AnalyticsEvent/ActorPseudonym and 43 §21 grants (the API roles cannot read pseudonym keys); deleting the key makes past events unlinkable (S8 acceptance).

global_decisions.decision: DSR execution: every module registers a PersonalDataHandler (export sections, erase). admin.dsr_export creates a data_export job (W8) that writes one encrypted CSV bundle (long format) owned by the user, delivered through DataExportFiles; admin.dsr_execute_deletion is 4EYES and its executor publishes user.deletion.requested; the worker consumer identity.dsr_deletion runs all erase handlers in one system transaction (idempotent), completes the request, publishes user.deletion.completed and revokes sessions. Authored public content stays under 'former member'.
global_decisions.reason: 41 §2.4 W8 "through each module's export interface", 52 DataSubjectRequest, MVP §14; module boundaries kept (GD-15).

global_decisions.decision: Environments: the development laptop and CI run lite mode only. Docker (full mode: Postgres + pgvector, Redis, NATS, OpenSearch, MinIO) runs on a test server; full-mode adapters are verified there, not in the scratch build.
global_decisions.reason: OQ-01 answered 2026-10-15: the local laptop is not capable enough for Docker.

global_decisions.decision: WebAuthn (passkeys and staff aal3 sign-in) uses @simplewebauthn/server (FIDO2 conformant, the TypeScript library of github.com/google/webauthndemo; behaviour checked against webauthn.io). Not written in-house. auth.webauthn_options and me.webauthn_register_options are built in S9.
global_decisions.reason: OQ-04 answered 2026-10-15; SEC-ADM-2 needs real staff aal3 sign-in.

global_decisions.decision: Media policy: videos are at most 15 seconds (all purposes). PDFs are never public and never reachable anonymously (no public URL, no anonymous link); authenticated fleet appointment sharing (GD-34) is the one exception that may include PDFs. HEIC is converted to JPEG automatically by the client before upload; the backend refuses image/heic at upload request as a safety net. Malware scanning, transcoding and PDF sanitizing keep the lite stand-ins.
global_decisions.reason: OQ-07 and OQ-08 answered and clarified 2026-10-15. Changes SEC-UP-2 (60 s -> 15 s) in Docs/40.

global_decisions.decision: VIN: lite decoder only (model year); one VIN has one owner across the platform (one non-archived vehicle per VIN, personal or fleet). Registering a VIN that is already owned answers 409 DUPLICATE with a transfer hint; the client asks 'Did you buy this car?' and, on yes, creates a vehicle transfer request to the previous owner (user, or fleet owner/manager for a fleet vehicle). The previous owner accepts or rejects; on acceptance every record connected to the vehicle (service records, documents, issues, reminders, media) moves to the new owner and the vehicle leaves the previous owner's garage. Requests expire if not answered; the previous owner's identity is not disclosed to the claimant before acceptance.
global_decisions.reason: OQ-10 answered and clarified 2026-10-15. Replaces 52 §8 'unique per owner, warning across owners'; adds transfer operations to Docs/40.

global_decisions.decision: Fleet vehicle data sharing: a provider sees a fleet vehicle's documents and service history only through an appointment for that vehicle; fleet managers are notified when sharing starts. A fleet owner or manager can mark a vehicle private, which stops sharing (appointments still work with the basic vehicle snapshot only). This sharing may include PDFs (the GD-32 exception). No organization-level vehicle_data_sharing consent.
global_decisions.reason: OQ-11 / DI-38 answered 2026-10-15.

global_decisions.decision: AI/MCP in the scratch build: the ai-mcp facade calls tools through McpClientPort; lite mode runs the MCP gateway in process with its own carpal_ai pool (AI output and registry reads only), a deterministic schema-valid stub (CARPAL_MCP_MODE=stub, dev default) or "unavailable" (staging/prod default until D6/D7 exist). Access logs are handed to W13 on the mcp.access_log queue; context packages come from the owning modules (AiContextSources); suggestions are applied by the owning modules (SuggestionAppliers).
global_decisions.reason: 41 §1 D6/D7 and §3.3 (own DB role for the gateway), SEC-AI-1..7; the real gateway and orchestrator are out of scope for S9.

global_decisions.decision: Contract sweep (S9b, 40 Appendix C, L22): tools/contract/contract-tests.ts generates one Vitest suite per module from operations.json (apps/testing/contract/generated, never edited by hand, checked by pnpm contract:check); each operation has a resolver in apps/testing/contract/resolvers/<module>.ts that builds its fixtures and the owner's call; the runner derives the generic checks (closed schemas, admin mechanics, same-organization BFLA, BOLA, kill switch, projection) from the registry, and the pipeline's CARPAL_VALIDATE_RESPONSES checks the success response. The guard-level BFLA matrix stays in routes.int.test.ts.
global_decisions.reason: Every operation is swept from the registry, so a new or changed operation cannot skip the contract tests; resolvers keep the requests real (linked records, plans, consents) without a schema-driven body synthesizer.

global_decisions.decision: OpenAPI is generated from the contract registry and schemas (tools/contract/openapi.ts), not from NestJS decorators (there are no controllers, GD-12); 40 "generated from NestJS" is read as "generated from the backend that serves it" and the equivalence is enforced by pnpm openapi:check against the registry and every host router.
global_decisions.reason: The router is generated from the same registry; one source for routes, schemas and the published description.

global_decisions.decision: fleet drivers are narrowed below ORG(ANY) on fleet records reached by id (WP0 narrowing, 40 §0.5): fleet media only when uploaded by them or attached to an assigned vehicle record (changes: own uploads only); fleet AI insights and suggestions never (404).
global_decisions.reason: User requirement of 2026-10-24: drivers, operators and mechanics see only the equipment linked to them; SEC-AZ-7.

global_decisions.decision: Search facets are counted by selecting each option's results from a second retrieval without the facetable filters, with the same selection code as the run (#collect / #select in search-service.ts); the run's own retrieval is unchanged. The facetable document filters are defined once (modules/discovery/domain/facets.ts) and used by search retrieval, facets and map.pins.
global_decisions.reason: Contract 1.1.0 promises that a count equals a run with that option and that facets never change results; deriving both from one selection function makes that true by construction (tested option by option).

global_decisions.decision: ProviderDoc.next_available_at looks 30 days ahead (ResultCard.next_available_slot, available_within_days up to 30); the 54 §5.1 operational fit counts it only within 14 days (ranking.rankingSlot), so scores are as before. A passed projected slot is re-read for cards in the caller's transaction and re-projected every 15 minutes (W15 SearchSlotRefreshRule).
global_decisions.reason: Contract 1.1.0 defines the card slot as the next 30 days and never in the past, while ranking must not change (54 §5.4).

folder_layout.backend/apps/: api, admin-api, auth, worker entry points (41 §1 D1-D3, D5). BFFs (D4) are deferred and live in backend/api-gateway/ later.
folder_layout.backend/libs/<lib>/: L1-L22 of 41 §2.2, one folder each: contract, http-pipeline, auth, authz, tenancy, idempotency, concurrency, rate-limit, outbox, jobs, crypto, link-tokens, i18n, flags, audit, consent-gate, entitlements, safety-check, geo, region-config, observability, testing. Add 'db' (Kysely pools, generated types) and 'infra' (ports + lite/full adapters).
folder_layout.backend/modules/<name>/: Layout of 41 §4.2: <name>.module.ts, interface/, api/, application/, domain/, infrastructure/, events/, projections/, tests/. Add modules/ai-mcp (missing from the skeleton).
folder_layout.backend/workers/<name>/: Handlers per worker (W1-W15 of 41 §2.4), registered in apps/worker. The existing folders (search-indexer, trust-scoring, notification-dispatch, analytics-pipeline, import-jobs) are kept; add others as the stages need them.
folder_layout.database/: tools/ (migration builder), migrations/ (generated + numbered), seeds/ (only if not covered by 43), policies/ (unused: RLS is inside 43).

conventions.naming: Operation handlers are bound by op id: @Operation('vehicles.create'). One use case class per operation in application/. Event types and payloads follow 40 Appendix A and 52 §20.
definition_of_done_per_operation: Handler bound to the op id, with request validation (closed schema) and the sec tags enforced by guards (auth, authz, flags, idempotency, ETag, rate-limit bucket, entitlement, consent, audit, as tagged).
Runs in one transaction with core.set_context(); writes only the module's own schema; cross-module reads go through interfaces.
Response is built by an allowlist projection for its audience (public, member or staff).
Documented operation-specific error codes are produced; events in its 'emit:' line are written to the outbox.
At least: one happy-path integration test, one authorization-negative test (BOLA or BFLA), plus a test per state-machine or business rule the op enforces.

commands_expected.test: pnpm test (unit) / pnpm test:int (integration, needs embedded DB)
commands_expected.db: pnpm db:setup | pnpm db:reset | pnpm db:codegen
commands_expected.contract: pnpm contract:generate | pnpm contract:check | pnpm contract:coverage
commands_expected.dev: pnpm dev (lite mode: api + admin-api + auth + embedded workers)

conventions.context_budget: Each stage should read only its listed doc ranges, lean on the generated registry (backend/libs/contract/generated/) instead of re-reading doc 40, and copy repetitive CRUD patterns from the first finished module rather than re-deriving them.

doc_issues.issue: 42.db schema.md calls itself 'Doc 41 (db schema)' and calls the script '42.db_setup.sql'. 41.backend plan.md links '41.db schema.md' and '42.db_setup.sql'. The actual files are 42.db schema.md and 43.db_setup.sql, and the script header says 'Doc 42'.
doc_issues.action: Code and tooling use the real file names. Suggest the user renumbers the references in 41/42/43.

doc_issues.issue: backend/README.md lists 15 modules. 41 §2.1 has 16 (M16 ai-mcp API facade). 41 §4.1 also has backend/apps/, which does not exist yet.
doc_issues.action: S1 creates backend/modules/ai-mcp and backend/apps/ and updates backend/README.md.
doc_issues.status: resolved in S1 (backend/apps/*, backend/modules/ai-mcp created; backend/README.md rewritten)

doc_issues.issue: Git tracks the folder as 'Docs/' but it appears as 'docs/' on this case-insensitive Windows disk.
doc_issues.action: Tooling must reference 'Docs/' exactly so it works on case-sensitive CI runners.

doc_issues.issue: 41 §4.1 puts migrations in database/migrations 'generated from 42.db_setup.sql', but 43 uses psql meta-commands (\set, \if, \gset, \connect) and cluster-level DDL (roles, two databases), so it cannot run through a plain driver.
doc_issues.action: S1.T4 builds a converter that resolves the meta-commands for env=dev|staging|prod and splits the output per database.
doc_issues.status: resolved in S1 (psql-compatible runner executes 43 directly; see GD-09 amendment)

doc_issues.issue: 40 admin.assist_session_start says staff call allowlisted operations "through {adm}/assist/{assist_session_id}/… with the same bodies as the portal", but does not say how the "…" suffix maps to the portal paths (e.g. is org.update reached at {adm}/assist/{id}/orgs/{org_id}?). The registry carries the 20 allowlisted op ids (assistAllowlist) but no assist routes.
doc_issues.action: S8 decides the mapping (proposal: the portal path after /v1, e.g. /v1/admin/assist/{assist_session_id}/orgs/{org_id}) and the doc is corrected.
doc_issues.s8_note: S8: assist sessions are started/ended and recorded, but the {adm}/assist/{assist_session_id}/… routes are still not in the registry, so staff cannot call the allowlisted operations yet. Proposal unchanged (portal path after /v1 under /v1/admin/assist/{id}/…); needs a 40 change and a router mapping (S9 or later).

doc_issues.issue: 40 auth.authorize declares q: client_id: Str without bounds (every other Str has <a,b>). The generator accepts it as a non-empty single-line string.
doc_issues.action: Suggest Str<3,40> to match the CarPal-Client client_id rule (40 §1.3).

doc_issues.issue: core.normalize_search_text() uses lower() and the regex class \s, which follow the database ctype: under the default -v db_locale=C only ASCII letters are lower-cased and only ASCII whitespace is collapsed (checked in S2). With C.UTF-8 or ICU the same function lower-cases Unicode and collapses Unicode spaces.
doc_issues.action: libs/i18n normalizeSearchText takes the DB locale (CARPAL_DB_LOCALE) and matches either behaviour; an integration test compares it with the database. Suggest 43 pins the behaviour (e.g. lower(... COLLATE "und-x-icu") and an explicit space class) so search keys do not depend on the install locale.

doc_issues.issue: core.publish_event() and analytics.write_audit() use INSERT ... RETURNING; the application roles have INSERT but no SELECT (and no SELECT policy) on core.domain_event_outbox / analytics.audit_logs, so publish_event failed for carpal_api, carpal_admin_api, carpal_auth, carpal_ai and write_audit for carpal_api, carpal_auth (42501).
doc_issues.action: Both functions are SECURITY DEFINER in Docs/43 (search_path already pinned; they only insert and read the caller's GUC context). 42 §5.3 lists them. Local databases: pnpm db:reset.

doc_issues.issue: admin.platform_role_revoke and admin.synonym_delete are DELETE operations with RSN, but DELETE takes no body (TR-6) and RSN means 'request body must contain reason'.
doc_issues.action: Decide in S8: make them POST .../revoke and POST .../delete with { reason }, or carry the reason in a header. A unit test pins the list of RSN operations whose input lacks reason.
doc_issues.s8_note: Decided: RSN DELETE operations take the reason from the CarPal-Reason header (40 §1.3 updated); 422 VALIDATION_FAILED at /reason when missing.

doc_issues.issue: Problem (40 §4.2) is a closed type, but CONSENT_REQUIRED ('body names the consent_type'), ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED ('body names the key') and PUBLISH_REQUIREMENTS_UNMET ('body lists missing requirements') need extra members.
doc_issues.action: S3/S4 decide: add optional members to Problem (e.g. consent_type, entitlement_key, requirements[]) or encode them as FieldErrors. The pipeline renders only the closed Problem today.
doc_issues.s3_note: S3 kept the closed Problem: CONSENT_REQUIRED names the consent type only in the internal detail (logs). Still to decide before S4 publishes profiles (PUBLISH_REQUIREMENTS_UNMET needs its list). Recommendation: add optional members consent_type, entitlement_key and requirements: List<Str<1,60>,20> to Problem in 40 §4.2 and regenerate.
doc_issues.s4_note: Problem (40 §4.2) gained optional members requirements: List<Str<1,60>,20>, consent_type: ConsentType, entitlement_key: Str<1,60>; contract regenerated; ApiError.extensions renders them; requireConsent/requireEntitlement and both publish operations set them.

doc_issues.issue: AAL2 is unreachable for accounts without a second factor, yet AAL2 guards the operations that enrol the first one (me.mfa_totp_enroll, me.webauthn_register_options) and everyday account operations (me.email_change, me.password_change, dsr.create, consent and onboarding operations). SEC-AU-10 defines aal2 as aal1 + second factor.
doc_issues.action: S3: a session records whether the account had an active second factor at sign-in (Session.mfaEnrolled); for sessions without one, a sign-in within the 10-minute step-up window satisfies AAL2 (re-authentication at the strongest level the account has). Staff, aal3 and enrolled accounts are unaffected. Suggest 40 SEC-AU-10 states this rule explicitly.

doc_issues.issue: 40 declares no type for six non-Id path parameters: flow_type (onboarding.update/accept_terms, admin.onboarding_reset), slug (public.org_get), report_type (fleet.report), role (admin.platform_role_revoke), key (admin.flag_update), dashboard_key (admin.analytics_dashboard). The generator treated them as Id, which made those routes unreachable with real values.
doc_issues.action: Generator default table (UNTYPED_PATH_PARAMS): OnboardingProgress['flow_type'], Slug, FleetReportType, Role, Str<1,80>, DashboardKey. Suggest adding `param:` lines (like provider.gated_decide) to those blocks in 40.

doc_issues.issue: auth.password_reset_complete lists "422 VALIDATION_FAILED(breached_password)", but FieldErrorCode (40 §4.2) has no code for a breached password.
doc_issues.action: S3 answers VALIDATION_FAILED with { pointer: "/new_password" (or /password), code: "pattern" }. Suggest adding a FieldErrorCode such as "not_allowed" or "breached".

doc_issues.issue: onboarding.update is ETAG (If-Match required), but a flow has no row, and so no version, before its first save.
doc_issues.action: S3: If-Match "v1" against a flow that does not exist yet creates it (version 1); any other version is 412. Suggest ETAG(if exists) for onboarding.update.

doc_issues.issue: 40 §6.2 does not say how the hosted sign-in UI returns to the client once AuthNext.next = "complete", and gives no error code for an unknown, expired or cookie-mismatched interaction_id.
doc_issues.action: S3: the hosted UI requests GET /oauth/authorize again with the same parameters; the __Host-cp_ia cookie names the completed interaction, so the server redirects to redirect_uri with code, state and iss (RFC 9207). Interaction errors are 410 LINK_EXPIRED (sign-in failures stay INVALID_CREDENTIALS). Suggest documenting both in 40 §6.2.

doc_issues.issue: me.email_change must not reveal whether the new address belongs to another account (202 always), so the conflict surfaces when the link is used; auth.email_verify lists only 410 errors.
doc_issues.action: S3: auth.email_verify answers 409 DUPLICATE when the new address was taken meanwhile (the link stays unused). Suggest adding "409 DUPLICATE" to auth.email_verify err.

doc_issues.issue: RLS made three S3 requirements impossible for the application roles: (a) the L16 consent gate must read another person's consent (a provider reading a vehicle owner's vehicle_data_sharing consent; grantee_read only covers records naming the organization, not unscoped ones); (b) consents.request_view/respond must answer LINK_RECIPIENT_MISMATCH for someone else's cn link, but party_all hides the request; (c) subscription.me_get "always at least Individual Free", but default_plan_insert admits organization subscribers only.
doc_issues.action: Docs/43 (+ 42 §5.3) gained three SECURITY DEFINER functions with minimal columns: identity.has_consent(subject, type, scope?, grantee?), identity.consent_request_by_token(hash), billing.ensure_user_subscription(user) (system context or the user themself). Local databases: pnpm db:reset.

doc_issues.issue: 52 §21 requires organization status active to publish a profile, but no operation of 40 moves an organization from draft to active (org.create must insert draft under RLS create_draft), and 56 §2.11 allows publishing with verification pending.
doc_issues.action: S4: provider.publish / vendor.publish activate a draft organization (draft|pending_verification|active may publish; suspended/archived/merged give organization_active in requirements). Suggest stating this in 40 provider.publish/vendor.publish and 52 §21.

doc_issues.issue: 40 OrgMember had user_id: Id and full_name: Str<2,100> (required), but org.members_list must list pending invitations, which have no user yet.
doc_issues.action: S4: Docs/40 OrgMember now has user_id: Id | null and full_name: Str<2,100> | null (email = invited address); contract regenerated.

doc_issues.issue: 52/40 do not say which default plan a hybrid_provider_vendor organization gets (billing plans have provider and vendor audiences only).
doc_issues.action: S4: hybrid starts on provider_basic (its public face is the provider profile); staff can reassign it. Product to confirm.

doc_issues.issue: Hybrid organizations: one membership per user and organization (role_memberships_org_uq), but {prv} routes need P* / P+ roles and {vnd} routes need V* / V+ roles, so the creator (provider_owner) cannot manage the vendor side; widening role groups is a contract change (40 §0.5).
doc_issues.action: Decide before the hybrid UI ships: e.g. in a hybrid organization provider_owner also satisfies V+/V* and vendor_owner P+/P*, or allow two memberships per user in hybrid organizations. S4 leaves the groups as written (workaround: invite a vendor_owner).
doc_issues.s8_note: S8: still undecided (no admin tooling changed role groups).

doc_issues.issue: org.member_update is ETAG but OrgMember carried no version, so clients could not send If-Match.
doc_issues.action: S4: Docs/40 OrgMember has version: Int<1,2147483647> (the membership row version); responses carry the ETag.

doc_issues.issue: identity.accept_invitation (Docs/43) set invitation_token_hash = NULL on acceptance, so a reused mi link was unknown (410 LINK_EXPIRED) and its own LINK_USED branch was unreachable; SEC-LT-4 requires 410 LINK_USED.
doc_issues.action: S4: Docs/43 keeps the hash on acceptance (the status check keeps the link single-use); revoking an invitation (member_remove) clears it. Local databases: pnpm db:reset.

doc_issues.issue: provider.portfolio_consent_request sends a cn link to the customer derived from a visit, but the business may not read the customer's contact data (SEC-OUT-3, RLS) and no event or operation delivers cn links.
doc_issues.action: S4: identity issues and mails the link itself; Docs/43 + 42 §5.3 gained identity.consent_request_contact(id) (definer): email/locale of the subject of a pending request of the caller's organization created in the same transaction. S6 may move delivery to the notification module (template identity.consent_request).

doc_issues.issue: 40 MediaAsset.status is 'active'|'quarantined'|'removed' but 52 MediaAsset has pending_upload, the state between upload_init and upload_complete.
doc_issues.action: S4: media.get answers 404 for pending_upload assets. Suggest adding pending_upload to MediaAsset.status in 40.

doc_issues.issue: 40 Url is https-only, but lite mode serves signed media URLs from the local http listener.
doc_issues.action: S4: the response check rewrites lite media URLs to an https placeholder (deviation); full mode uses the https media host. No contract change needed.

doc_issues.issue: 40 provider.coverage_create says each row is validated independently, but NodeId<type> checks (GD-17) run for the whole body in the pipeline, so one unknown node rejects the batch.
doc_issues.action: S4: parent chains and duplicates are per row (skipped codes); node existence/type is per request. Suggest 40 states that NodeId errors fail the whole request.

doc_issues.issue: S4 plan said provider.insights_get answers 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE until S9, but the operation has no FLAG and is not an AI feature; most of its figures belong to trust, appointment and analytics (S6-S8).
doc_issues.action: S4: implemented with this module's figures and 0/null from OrganizationExtensions.registerInsight until those modules register. Suggest marking which ProviderInsights/VendorInsights figures are nullable before their source exists.

doc_issues.issue: 40 HoursSpec day_of_week: Int<0,6> does not say which day is 0 (the pilot region's week starts on Saturday).
doc_issues.action: S4: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday (JavaScript getDay) in openNow. Suggest stating it in 40 §7.1.

doc_issues.issue: 40 OrgUpdate.slug allows at most 2 changes per 30 days, but no column records slug changes and no error code is named.
doc_issues.action: S4: counted in the KV store (30-day TTL), 429 RATE_LIMITED when exceeded. Suggest a slug_changed_at history (or audit read) and naming the code.

doc_issues.issue: 52 OrganizationLocation: exactly one primary per organization, but 40 LocationWrite.is_primary is a free boolean and does not say what happens to the first location or when the primary is deactivated.
doc_issues.action: S4: the first active location becomes primary; a second primary is 422 /is_primary not_unique; deactivating the primary promotes the oldest other active location, or 409 INVALID_TRANSITION(primary_location) when it is the only one.

doc_issues.issue: 40 writes ORG(FC) DRV on issues.create and vehicles.mileage_add and says a fleet driver's report starts the approval workflow, but FC (fleet_owner, fleet_manager, fleet_maintenance_coordinator) excludes fleet_driver, so read as "ORG(FC) and DRV" no driver could ever call them.
doc_issues.action: S5: DRV widens the alternative to fleet drivers on assigned vehicles (GD-20). Suggest 40 §0.4 say so explicitly ("DRV: fleet drivers are allowed in addition to the listed roles, limited to assigned vehicles").

doc_issues.issue: 40 Job.result is optional ("set when succeeded"), but 52/43 require result_type and result_id for every succeeded job and JobResultType has no value for bulk_inventory_update, which only changes existing items.
doc_issues.action: S5: Docs/43 check relaxed for kind bulk_inventory_update (and result_type/result_id now set together); Docs/42 notes it. Suggest 52 BackgroundJob.result_type say "required when succeeded, except bulk_inventory_update".

doc_issues.issue: Docs/43 inventory.tg_inquiry_rules let the vendor move a reserved inquiry to cancelled, but the 40 §13.1 table gives the vendor only answered, unavailable and completed from reserved.
doc_issues.action: S5: trigger aligned with 40 (Docs/43, Docs/42 §6); the API checks the same table first.

doc_issues.issue: 40 §3.3 lets POST searches page in their bodies (inventory.search, search.run, public.org_inventory_search …), but the S2 pipeline only verified and bound query-string cursors.
doc_issues.action: S5: pipeline verifies body cursors and binds them to the body filters (GD-12 amendment).

doc_issues.issue: Maintenance reminders and document expiry need notifications (41 §6.3 hourly rule, Plan WP5), but 40 Appendix A / 50 §20 name no event for them; likewise no event when a stock-inquiry reservation expires.
doc_issues.action: S5 publishes vehicle.reminder.due (payload reminder_id via aggregate, vehicle_id, status due|overdue, reminder_type, owner_type, owner_id) when a reminder becomes due or overdue; reservation expiry publishes nothing yet. Suggest adding vehicle.reminder.due (and inquiry.reservation.expired if the requester should be told) to Appendix A and 50 §20 before S6 builds the notification consumers. S7 adds appointment.reminder.due the same way (DI-54).
doc_issues.s6_note: S6: the notification dispatcher consumes vehicle.reminder.due (user owner → service_reminder; fleet owner → vehicle_due_for_service to FC roles). The event is still missing from 40 Appendix A.

doc_issues.issue: 40 §4.4 VIN_INVALID covers "format or check-digit rules", but the ISO 3779 check digit is mandatory only for North American (WMI 1-5) and Chinese (L) VINs; pilot-region VINs (WMI N*) use position 9 freely, so a strict check would refuse real vehicles.
doc_issues.action: S5: format always; check digit only for WMI 1-5 and L (modules/vehicle/domain/vin.ts). Suggest 52 §8 state the rule.

doc_issues.issue: vehicle_data_sharing is a personal consent (52 ConsentRecord: organization subjects only for the three *_ai_use types), but fleet vehicles belong to an organization: 40 does not say how a fleet shares documents or service history with a provider, or how a provider logs work on a fleet vehicle.
doc_issues.action: S5: a fleet shares its own documents by its coordinators' decision (FC role, no consent record); provider.service_record_create and job-log vehicle links fail closed (403 CONSENT_REQUIRED) for fleet vehicles. Needs a decision in S7/S8 (e.g. an organization-subject vehicle_data_sharing, or appointments as the only path for fleets). S7: fleet appointment requests ignore share_history (DI-58); providers record work on fleet vehicles through appointments (provider.service_record_create with appointment_id needs no consent).
doc_issues.s8_note: S8: fleets still share history with providers only through appointments (no organization-subject vehicle_data_sharing); fleet approvals are now bound to appointments. Decision still needed (OQ-11).

doc_issues.issue: 52 VehicleIssue.description is 10–3000 characters; 40 IssueWrite.description is Text<3000> without a minimum.
doc_issues.action: S5: the 52 minimum is enforced by the use case (422 /description too_short, limit 10). Suggest Text<10,3000> in 40.

doc_issues.issue: 52 Vehicle.profile_completeness (S, 0–100) and InventoryItem.data_quality_score have no weights; 54 §7.2 lists the data-quality criteria only; 54 §3.2/§7.2 name inquiry_fulfillment_rate without a definition.
doc_issues.action: S5: equal weights (vehicle: 12 optional criteria + brand/model/year; item: images, part numbers, category, warranty note, description, stock status); inquiry_fulfillment_rate = share of the last 90 days' decidable inquiries the vendor answered within 24 h without marking them unavailable (requester cancellations before an answer and fresh unanswered ones excluded). See OQ-09 for the same question about profiles. S7: the vendor trust score uses the measured inquiry response time for inquiry responsiveness (54 §3.2) until inquiry_fulfillment_rate is defined.

doc_issues.issue: 40 ImportCreate.column_mapping.field is Str<1,60> with no list of target fields, and gives no way to name a part category other than its node id.
doc_issues.action: S5: fields are the InventoryItemWrite members with translations per locale (name_translations.en …; modules/inventory/domain/import-row.ts IMPORT_FIELDS); categories by node id only. Suggest an enum in 40 and a category-by-slug or label option (or the S9 AI classify_category).

doc_issues.issue: 40 vehicles.vin_reveal lists no error for a vehicle without a VIN; vin_decode uses 409 INVALID_TRANSITION(no_vin).
doc_issues.action: S5: vin_reveal answers 404 NOT_FOUND for a vehicle without a VIN. Suggest listing 409 INVALID_TRANSITION(no_vin) like vin_decode.

doc_issues.issue: InventoryItem.data_quality_score and the missing_images filter depend on image attachments, which the media module owns and changes without an event (media.attach / detach / delete).
doc_issues.action: S5: scores are recomputed on every item write, after imports and by the daily W15 rule inventory.catalog_quality; missing_images asks media per page. Suggest a media.attachment.changed event (or an attach hook through AttachmentTargets) so owning modules can react.

doc_issues.issue: 40 inquiries.vendor_get is CNS(vendor_fitment_context: for vehicle snapshot) without saying whether a missing consent refuses the read or hides the snapshot; 41 §6.3 says expired reservations are "released" without the target status.
doc_issues.action: S5: the inquiry is always readable by the vendor; the snapshot is null while the consent is missing or withdrawn (checked on every read). An expired reservation goes back to answered (still open) with reserved_until cleared.

doc_issues.issue: 40 Appendix A lacks events S6 needs: unpublication and vendor publication (only provider.profile.published exists), profile/location edits for the search indexer, community content changes, post publication for followers, reaction counts for counters other modules own, and the in-app security alert of SEC-AU-5.
doc_issues.action: S6 publishes provider.profile.unpublished, vendor.profile.published, vendor.profile.unpublished, organization.profile.updated {change: profile|location|organization}, community.content.changed {entity_type, entity_id}, community.post.published {organization_id, post_type}, community.reaction.changed {target_type, target_id, reaction_type, count} and user.security_alert {user_id, kind}; vendor.inventory.imported gained requested_by_user_id. Suggest adding them to Appendix A and 50 §20.

doc_issues.issue: 40 search.page declares only `q: cursor: Cursor` (required), so the page size cannot be chosen and the first request needs a cursor.
doc_issues.action: S6: pages after the first hold 20 results; the cursor comes from search.run / search.refine (ctx.cursorFor). Suggest `q: cursor: Cursor, limit?` like other lists.
doc_issues.resolution: Docs/40 1.1.0: search.page takes q: cursor: Cursor, limit?: Int<1,50>=20, and the new search.session_get reads the first page of a session (pwa DI-46). S10.T2.

doc_issues.issue: 40 questions.update is ETAG but PublicQuestion carries no version, so a client cannot learn the value for If-Match.
doc_issues.action: S6: questions.create / get / update send the ETag header ("v<version>") even though the body has no version. Suggest adding version to PublicQuestion (author view) or dropping ETAG.

doc_issues.issue: 40 SearchMode has showcases and qna, but ResultCard.target is organization or inventory_item only; showcases and questions have their own reads (showcases.get, questions.search).
doc_issues.action: S6: search_mode showcases and qna rank providers like providers mode (the match session records the mode). Suggest dropping the two modes from SearchRequest or defining their result cards.

doc_issues.issue: 40 SearchRequest.issue_id links a search to a vehicle issue, but nothing says how it changes the search (symptom context, urgency) and the vehicle module exposes no issue read for other modules.
doc_issues.action: S6: issue_id is not stored or used (MatchSession.issue_id null); the urgency_level of the body and the safety check apply. S7 (Help Me / appointments from issues) should add a VehicleCards issue read and use the issue's symptom as a chip.

doc_issues.issue: Json<MatchReasonValues>, Json<FeedCard> and Json<TemplateParams> are server-defined schemas (x-server-schema) that 40 never writes down.
doc_issues.action: S6 shapes: MatchReasonValues = plain values per reason_type (level, jobs, system/task/brand node ids, offered, covered, avg_rating, reviews, distance_km, response_minutes/target, matching_items, fitment_confidence, in_stock_items, stock_status, urgency_level, fast, favorite, verified, badge); FeedCard per kind (organization card + distance; post excerpt; reminder title/type/status; showcase title, organization, thumbnail; question title/status/answer_count); TemplateParams = the template's placeholders (domain/templates.ts). Suggest documenting them in 40 and validating them (S9 OpenAPI).
doc_issues.resolution: Written down as OpenAPI components in shared/api-contracts/openapi.yaml (generated; AI payloads and event properties from their validating schemas).

doc_issues.issue: answers.delete of an accepted answer: the answer's author may not change another user's question (RLS author_all), so the accepted reference cannot be cleared, and 40 names no error.
doc_issues.action: S6: deleting an accepted answer is 409 INVALID_TRANSITION(accepted_answer). Suggest either a definer that reopens the question or documenting the 409.

doc_issues.issue: notification.push_device_tokens.token_hash is unique across users, but a device that signs into another account registers the same token while the old row belongs to the previous user (invisible under RLS).
doc_issues.action: S6: the second account gets 409 DUPLICATE (/token not_unique); sign-out should revoke the token (push_tokens.revoke). Suggest a definer that moves the token to the new account, or revocation on session end (S9 hardening).

doc_issues.issue: 40 SearchFilters.available_within_days and preferred_partners_only depend on availability (S7) and fleet preferred partners (S8); public.availability computes slots from availability rules that do not exist yet.
doc_issues.action: S6: available_within_days is ignored, preferred_partners_only fails closed (no results), public.availability answers { slots: [] } after checking the provider and location. S7/S8 replace them. S7: public.availability computes slots; available_within_days filters providers by their indexed next open slot (providers without a calendar are left out); preferred_partners_only still fails closed until S8.
doc_issues.s8_note: S8: preferred_partners_only now returns the searching fleet's active preferred providers (as_organization_id), and the +5 fleet preferred-partner bonus applies.

doc_issues.issue: 40 Appendix A lacks events S7 needs: appointment reminders, notes, delays and calendar changes, review edits/removals, response publication, invitation reminders, dispute opening and stock-inquiry status changes (requesters cannot be told about answers otherwise).
doc_issues.action: S7 publishes appointment.reminder.due, appointment.note_added, appointment.delay_reported, appointment.availability.changed, review.edited, review.removed, review.response.published, review.response.removed, review.invitation.reminded, dispute.opened and inquiry.status_changed with id-only payloads. Add them to Appendix A and 52 §20.

doc_issues.issue: 40 appointments.create names no error for the SEC-BF-3 open-request caps and the no-show cooldown, and no values for them.
doc_issues.action: S7 answers 429 RATE_LIMITED (retry-after 3600) at 3 open requests per provider, 10 in total, or within 7 days after a no-show at that provider (proposed values).

doc_issues.issue: 52 §12 requires a capacity check at confirmation, but a provider without availability rules has no capacity defined; 40 does not say whether such providers can confirm.
doc_issues.action: S7: a location without any active rule has no calendar; confirmation checks only time off (same advisory lock) and public.availability offers no slots. Product to confirm.

doc_issues.issue: 40 Appointment.requester_contact is "for the requester's preferred channel", but in_app and push have no address and many users set no preference.
doc_issues.action: S7 (definer appointment.requester_contact): the verified email when the preference is email or unset, the verified phone for sms, otherwise null.

doc_issues.issue: 40 AppointmentCreate.share_history creates personal consents, but fleet requests have no personal consent subject for fleet vehicles (see DI-38).
doc_issues.action: S7 ignores share_history for fleet requests (consent_to_share_history false); decide with DI-38 / OQ-11.

doc_issues.issue: 40 review_responses.update says a published response is "re-moderated", but ReviewResponse has no moderation status.
doc_issues.action: S7 keeps an edited published response published; S8 moderation may add a status or a queue entry.

doc_issues.issue: 54 §9.4 publishes trust.score.changed only for changes above 5 points, but the search index (W2) needs every change to rank by the current score.
doc_issues.action: S7 publishes trust.score.changed on every change and audits only changes above 5 points (and the first score).

doc_issues.issue: 52 ProviderCapabilityEvidence.base_weight is an integer (smallint in 43), but 54 §1.1 review weights are fractional for Path 2 (8 × 0.6 = 4.8, 4 × 0.6 = 2.4).
doc_issues.action: S7 rounds (5 and 2). Change the column to numeric(5,2) in a numbered migration if calibration needs exact weights.

doc_issues.issue: 40 admin.flag_update, admin.mcp_client_update and admin.taxonomy_node_update are ETAG, but FeatureFlag, McpClientView and TaxonomyNode had no version, so clients could not send If-Match.
doc_issues.action: S8: Docs/40 gained version on FeatureFlag and McpClientView and an optional version on TaxonomyNode (staff responses); contract regenerated.

doc_issues.issue: 40 Appendix A lacks events S8 needs: feature_flag.changed (flag cache bust in every process), user.deletion.requested (approved deletion handed to the worker), dsr.deadline.approaching (staff alert); fleet.approval.requested from provider.appointments_update has no approval yet (the fleet decides by threshold).
doc_issues.action: S8 publishes them with id-only/plain payloads; fleet.approval.requested carries approval_id when an approval exists (W5 notifies only those). Add them to Appendix A and 52 §20.

doc_issues.issue: 52 Notification.event_type has no type for fleet approval decisions, DSR deadline alerts or verification outcomes.
doc_issues.action: S8 uses system_announcement (fleet decisions), moderation_alert (DSR deadlines) and moderation_update (moderation outcomes, verification, location corrections). Suggest fleet_approval_decided, dsr_deadline_alert and verification_decided in 52 and 43.

doc_issues.issue: 40 admin.analytics_dashboard takes region and organization_type filters, but 43 events.daily_metrics aggregates have a free dimension_key and 52 names no dimensions.
doc_issues.action: S8 stores aggregates without dimensions and ignores both filters. Decide the dimensions (region, org type, platform) before dashboards are used.

doc_issues.issue: 40 admin.user_status suspend_until has no rule that lifts the suspension, and 52 UserAccount has no suspended_until column.
doc_issues.action: S8 records it on the moderation action only. Suggest a column or a W15 rule reading moderation actions.

doc_issues.issue: 40 admin.org_merge says references are re-pointed, but no module interface lists organization references (memberships, locations, profiles, reviews, appointments …), and unique keys collide.
doc_issues.action: S8 marks the duplicate merged and unpublishes it; references resolve through merged_into_organization_id. Needs an OrganizationReferences registry (like TaxonomyReferences) with per-module conflict rules.

doc_issues.issue: 40 admin.dispute_resolve: for review_approval_objection, 52 §11 says an upheld objection publishes the review with disputed_by_business, i.e. 'upheld' means the review is upheld, not the business's objection.
doc_issues.action: S8 follows 52: resolved_upheld publishes (reviewer decision approved by the dispute decider, reason objection_upheld); resolved_rejected rejects the review. Suggest wording in 40 that names the outcome for the review explicitly.

doc_issues.issue: 43 media.media_assets.mime_type allows images, video, PDF and CSV only, so a DSR export bundle cannot be JSON.
doc_issues.action: S8 writes the bundle as one CSV in long format (section, record_id, field, value). Suggest allowing application/json (or zip) for system_export if a structured bundle is required.

doc_issues.issue: 40 VinDecodeResult.suggested was Partial<VehicleWrite>, which includes vin: the closed response schema of vehicles.vin_decode admitted a full VIN although SEC-OUT-2 allows it only from vehicles.vin_reveal.
doc_issues.action: S9b changed 40 to Partial<Omit<VehicleWrite,'vin'>> and regenerated libs/contract/generated; the static projection test checks that only vehicles.vin_reveal can return a VIN.

doc_issues.issue: 40 vehicles.status_history, appointments.history and appointments.notes_list were USR | ORG(F*) without DRV; F* contains fleet_driver, so a driver could read the status history of any fleet vehicle (SEC-AZ-7). Fleet records reached by id (media, AI records, ORG(ANY)) had no driver rule.
doc_issues.action: S9c added DRV to the three operations and extended SEC-AZ-7 (drivers: fleet media only when uploaded by them or attached to an assigned vehicle record, no fleet AI records); regenerated the contract, the sweep suites and the OpenAPI file.

doc_issues.issue: Contract gaps found by the consumer PWA in its stage P6 (pwa/dev_plan.json DI-42..DI-46): (1) SearchResponse had no counts per filter option, so the filter panel could not show counts and the filters-too-narrow state could not name the filter that removed most results; (2) no 'Soonest available' sort; (3) MapPin had no slug or card fields, so a pin could not open its profile or request step without a matching search card; (4) map.pins ignored filters.open_now and available_within_days, so Open now could only be filtered in the browser, and server clusters still counted closed places; (5) the first page of a search session could not be read again, so a reload ran the search again.
