notes_for_next: Run every command from backend/ after `source tools/use-local-node.sh`. `pnpm test:int` starts the DB and runs db:setup by itself (idempotent).

Registry (loadRegistry()): each Route has host (api | admin-api | auth | storage), method, path with {param} placeholders (convert to :param for Nest/Express), pathParams, and security = { principals: SecTag[][] (ANY ONE alternative, each an AND-list of PUB/USR/ORG/DRV/STF/LNK), tags: SecTag[] (ALL apply) }. SecTag = { tag, args, qualifier? }. Dual-scope ops ({V}/{A}/{RQ}) are two routes with scope me | fleet | org. Single-path ops with "USR | ORG(...)" have two principal alternatives where the org is resolved by target or body (media.*, jobs.*, ai.insight_*), qualifier "by target"/"by approver_role" on ai.suggestion_decide / ai.approval_decide.

Special routes: media.upload_put has host "storage" and no principals (signed URL; not a Nest route). auth.token and auth.revoke have inputEncoding "form" (RFC 6749); auth.authorize answers 302. Operations with alternateResponses (admin.flag_update, admin.mcp_client_update) can answer 202 PendingChange (4EYES).

Schemas: createContractAjv() returns a strict Ajv2020 with all $defs registered; per-op schemas in loadSchemas().operations[opId] = { input?, response?, alternateResponses?, query (closed object; cursor/limit shorthand expanded, admin limit ≤ 100), pathParams }. Custom keywords: x-node-type (TaxonomyResolver check, S3), x-conditional (the "// C:" rule text; enforced by the owning use case), x-server-schema (Json<Name>: server-defined schemas still to be written by the owning module), x-external (RFC-defined OAuth/OIDC/WebAuthn documents), x-locale-config.

Error catalog (ERROR_CODES, 50 codes with status and common flag), ENUMS (75 from §5), ROLE_GROUPS (15; O+ and M+ are orgTypeRelative, ANY = any active member) and the OperationId union type are exported from #libs/contract/index.js.
Kysely: import type { DB } from #libs/db/index.js; table keys are "schema.table"; numeric and date columns are strings, timestamptz are Date. Regenerate with pnpm db:codegen after any DB change.

Request context: SELECT core.set_context(actor_type, user_id, org_id, role, request_id, anon_key) first in every transaction (transaction-local). carpal_api is refused system/staff (SQLSTATE 42501); staff is only for carpal_admin_api; system for carpal_auth/worker/ai.

Test DB strategy for S2.T14: roles are cluster-wide, but the per-role settings (search_path = pg_catalog, core, ext; statement/lock timeouts) are set IN DATABASE carpal. A database cloned with CREATE DATABASE … TEMPLATE carpal does NOT inherit them, so either re-apply the ALTER ROLE … IN DATABASE statements for clones or use per-test transactions with rollback on the main carpal database. Login role passwords default to <role>_dev.

NestJS 12 is not installed yet. Check early in S2 that DI works under ESM with tsc emitDecoratorMetadata (build) and unplugin-swc (tests); eslint consistent-type-imports is already off in apps/modules/workers because Nest injects by class.

Principal alternatives (A | B) with PUB / PUB(no token) / USR / ORG(groups[:qualifier]) / DRV / STF(roles) / LNK; tags AAL2/AAL3 (conditional ones with arguments are left to the use case), PURP (header format; 400 if missing/malformed, 404 if the PurposeVerifier refuses), ATT. DRV restricts fleet_driver only (assignment to the path vehicle via DriverAssignments; driverScoped flag otherwise). Failures: 401 for a missing user, otherwise 404 (never 403). notes_for_next: Writing a handler: a Nest provider with @Operation('<op.id>') and handle(ctx). ctx gives params, query (typed, defaults applied), body (validated, normalized), principal, access (AccessGrant: org {id,type,role}, matchedGroups, qualifiers, driverScoped, deferredOrg, link, purpose, conditionalAssurance), locale, ifMatch, cursor, and helpers tx(fn), authorizeOrg(orgId, groups), requireAssurance(level), flagEnabled(key), rateLimit(bucket, scope, key, cost), page(items, nextPosition). Return { status?, body, headers?, cache?, contentLanguage? }; throw ApiError(code[, {errors, detail}]). The module must be imported in apps/shared/app-modules.ts.

Transactions: ctx.tx(async (scope) => ...) sets core.set_context(actor, user, path org, role, request id, anon key). Use scope.setOrganization(orgId, role) after ctx.authorizeOrg for 'by target' operations. publishEvent(scope, {...}) and writeAudit(scope, {...}) write in the same transaction; with CARPAL_VALIDATE_RESPONSES (default in dev/test) an AUD operation that wrote no audit entry and any response that violates the contract answer 500. Jobs: JobService.create(scope, ...) + acceptedJob(row).

Register meaningful constraint names with registerConstraintErrors({name: 'DUPLICATE' | {code, pointer}}) (libs/db). The SQLSTATE mapping already covers P0410/P0411/P0403/P0409, INVALID_TRANSITION/TAXONOMY_MISMATCH message prefixes, RLS write violations (-> 404) and timeouts (-> 503 with retry).

report.summary: Identity, the auth server, billing and taxonomy are implemented: 55 of the 58 S3 operations (3 WebAuthn/social operations deferred). Users sign up, verify, sign in with a password or a one-time code, add a TOTP second factor with recovery codes, get DPoP-bindable tokens through authorization code + PKCE, refresh with rotation and family revocation, and manage their account, preferences, memberships, sessions, consents (incl. business consent requests via cn links), data subject requests and onboarding. Plans, subscriptions, change requests and a race-safe entitlement check exist, and user.registered creates Individual Free through the worker. The taxonomy is served from an in-memory catalog with typeahead, the NodeId<type> request check and the safety lexicon. All platform ports S2 left open for S3 are bound (ConsentChecker, EntitlementChecker, SafetyLexicon, TaxonomyVersion, AttestationVerifierPort, MembershipDirectory). Docs/43 gained three definer functions; two contract-generator gaps from S1 were fixed.

Handler habits: `caller(ctx)` (identity application/common.ts) or `ctx.principal.kind === "user"`; path org = ctx.access.org (authorized); writes in ctx.tx(async (scope) => …); ETAG ops compare row.version with ctx.ifMatch on a FOR UPDATE read; Page responses = ctx.page(items, next) with a small position object ({ id } keyset on UUIDv7 ids, or { o } offset); register meaningful unique/check constraints with registerConstraintErrors; publishEvent/writeAudit inside the same tx; side effects after commit with scope.afterCommit.

Response validation (CARPAL_VALIDATE_RESPONSES, on in tests) catches projection mistakes at once (e.g. arrays of domain types such as core.country[] arrive as "{…}" text: use textArray from #libs/db). Keep it on.

Platform ports now bound: ConsentChecker (identity, definer function; pass grantee { type: "organization", id } to restrict to one recipient), EntitlementChecker (billing; call requireEntitlement(checker, scope, subscriber, key, delta, { usage? }) BEFORE the insert inside the write tx), SafetyLexicon + SafetyCheck (taxonomy; inject SafetyCheck), TaxonomyVersion, NodeTypeChecker, AttestationVerifierPort (PoW), MembershipDirectory. Still stubs: DriverAssignments (S8 fleet), PurposeVerifier (S8 admin).

Extension points to fill (GD-15): billing UsageCounters.register("max_vehicles" | "max_inventory_items", counter) in onModuleInit (S5); identity ConsentScopes.register("vehicle" | "appointment" | "media_asset" | "portfolio_item" | "stock_inquiry", ownerCheck) (S4/S5/S7); identity DataExportFiles provider (media, S4/S8); OrgCards logo_url (S4).

TaxonomyResolver (#modules/taxonomy/interface/taxonomy-resolver.js): NodeId<type> body fields are already checked by the pipeline; use requireDescendant for chains (model under brand, series under model), labels(ids, locale) for public L10n labels, canonicalId to follow merges, mappingsFrom for triage/matching. Call invalidate() after admin taxonomy changes (S8) and publish taxonomy.node.merged after merges.

Auth server facts for later stages: sessions are server-side (SessionStore) and every refresh-token family is one session; SessionStore.revokeAll(userId) ends everything (use it for suspension, DSR deletion, password reset); Authorizer.invalidateUser/invalidateOrganization after membership, role or status changes (SEC-AU-3). Staff tokens for tests: fixtures.token(user, { staff: true }).

Test harness additions: createTestApp({ host, infra }) with one shared infra when sessions or mail must cross hosts; app.mail(to, template?) / app.sms(to) read the lite sinks; fixtures.withPassword(user, pw), fixtures.subscription(org, planKey, { vehicleLimit }), fixtures.token(user, { acr, authTime, mfaEnrolled }), fixtures.worker (carpal_worker system tx) to run consumers or assert outbox rows; handlerModule handlers override real ones. Integration tests must live in apps/testing (modules may not import apps). The SEC-AU-11 latency floor is 0 in tests by default.

Worker tests: drain deterministically (relay.settle(), relay.drainOnce(), infra.bus.idle()) instead of polling. In two early full runs the first version of the user.registered worker test hung for 60 s under one file ordering; it could not be reproduced afterwards (five full runs green) and the deterministic version has passed every run. If a worker test hangs again, check pending outbox rows and consumer retries first.

Contract notes: 40 still has open doc issues DI-05, DI-07, DI-09, DI-10 (decide before S4 publish), DI-11..DI-16. OAuth endpoints answer RFC 6749 JSON errors through ProtocolError (not Problem); the OpenAPI file (S9) must describe them.

report.summary: All 71 API operations of §7, §8, §9 and §17 are implemented (the 72nd, media.upload_put, is the signed PUT served by the storage listener). Users create organizations (draft, owner membership, default plan of the audience in the same transaction), invite members by single-use mi links, manage roles with the last-owner rule, add locations by exact pin with the pin-versus-address check and the 0.01° public point, use the location editor (lite geocoder, SSRF-safe map links) and submit verifications with clean private documents. Providers complete and publish their profile (PUBLISH_REQUIREMENTS_UNMET names the missing rules through the new optional Problem.requirements, DI-10; publication activates a draft organization, DI-18), maintain certifications, service catalog, coverage and capabilities with parent-chain checks and the AI approval gate, log jobs (vehicle links consent-gated), keep private customer notes and publish portfolio items only with a clean attachment and the customer's showcase consent obtained by a cn link. Vendors publish with coverage and "catalog coming soon". Media runs end to end in lite mode: upload_init → signed PUT → upload_complete → W6 (byte sniffing, EICAR stand-in scan, sharp re-encode without EXIF, display/thumbnail variants, encryption at rest) → media.scan.completed; attachments ask the owning module, delivery URLs are signed per viewer. Public projections (PublicProfiles) are ready for S6. Contract/DB fixes: Problem members, OrgMember (nullable user fields, version), identity.accept_invitation (LINK_USED) and identity.consent_request_contact.

report.summary: All 61 operations of §12 (31) and §13.2-13.3 (30) are implemented. Owners and fleets manage vehicles under {me}/vehicles and {flt}/vehicles: the active-vehicle limit is checked under the subscriber lock in the write transaction (six parallel creates at 4 of 5 → exactly one succeeds), the VIN is normalized, checked (check digit only where mandatory), stored as an AES-256-GCM envelope with a keyed hash and its last four characters, and returned only by vin_reveal (AAL2, audited); duplicates are refused per owner and flagged across owners. Item data quality and the catalog quality score (54 §7.2) are computed and stored on the vendor profile; InventoryRead gives S6 the public item projections with trade prices only for approved trade customers. The S4 fail-closed paths opened: service-record visits (job logs inherit customer_confirmed / invoice_verified / appointment_verified), the customer check, vehicle owners for consent gates, the vendor item counter and vendor insights. Community: follows, favourites, posts with publication rules, comments, reactions counted without the subject organization's members (definer community.refresh_reaction_count), Q&A with business answers and the accepted answer; text pre-moderated (GD-22). Notifications: list, unread count, read marks, preferences (defaults, digests, marketing consent), encrypted push tokens, and W5 dispatch with EN/FA templates for the S3-S6 events (security alert as a critical in-app notice, identity and invitation mails rendered through the Messenger). An appointment created from an issue schedules the issue when the request is sent (requester context), not at confirmation: the provider cannot read the customer's issues.
The completion service record drops inventory references from parts (the provider names its parts) and is written only when a service system is known (body or appointment).

report.summary: All 82 S8 operations are implemented: §18 fleet (20), §22 events.ingest and reports.create, and the §23 admin plane (60, including the 4 MCP/AI oversight data operations). The admin plane runs only on admin-api with aal3 staff sessions, purpose-bound reads with pii.read audit entries, four-eyes changes executed by registered executors in the approver's transaction, moderation (reports, cases, actions on content owned by other modules through ModerationTargets, an intake rule for held content), Path 2 reviewer decisions, disputes, badge approval, verification, location correction, organization status and merges, billing and taxonomy administration (merge job re-pointing references), flags with the kill switch, retention, audit search, MCP records and assist sessions. DSRs are executed: W8 builds a per-user export bundle from every module's PersonalData handler, and an approved deletion erases/anonymizes across modules in the worker, deletes the analytics pseudonym key and publishes user.deletion.completed. Analytics: events.ingest → W12 (pseudonymized) → daily metrics and dashboards. Fleets: profile (activates the fleet), dashboard, driver assignments (drivers now reach assigned vehicles), partners (search filter and ranking bonus), approvals wired into driver issues, fleet appointments and provider cost estimates, reports, CSV exports (W8) and vehicle imports (W7). Remaining W15 rules (trials, DSR deadlines, expiry, retention, jobs) are scheduled. The four acceptance criteria are covered by integration tests.

ai.suggestions_list, ai.suggestions_mine and ai.approvals_list default to status pending when no status is given.

parts.title: Contract test sweep (L22 generator over all operations)
steps: S9b.1 Generator from operations.json + schemas: one generated suite per module under apps/testing/contract (or tests/contract), with per-op fixtures resolvers (owner, other tenant, anonymous, wrong role, staff).
S9b.2 Schema conformance of every success response; BOLA matrix (other user / other organization -> 404) and BFLA matrix (role below the sec line -> 404/401) for every operation.
S9b.3 Admin-plane mechanics: staff client cp-web-admin with aal3, purpose resolver for PURP routes, 202 PendingChange for 4EYES, CarPal-Reason for RSN DELETEs, pii.read audit for staff PII responses.
S9b.4 Projection tests for SEC-OUT-1 fields (no credentials, token hashes, VINs or private fields in public/staff views); kill switch -> AI 503 while search, profiles and appointments succeed.
S9b.5 Fix the defects the sweep finds in S3-S9a modules (budgeted work, not optional); record each in the deviations or the report.

report.summary: S9b built the contract sweep of 40 Appendix C over the whole API surface. tools/contract/contract-tests.ts generates one suite per module (apps/testing/contract/generated/<module>.contract.int.test.ts, 17 files, every HTTP route of operations.json except the storage PUT); pnpm contract:check fails when they are stale. Each operation has a resolver (apps/testing/contract/resolvers/<module>.ts, 406 of them, branching per route scope for the {V}/{A}/{RQ}/{VT} aliases) that builds real fixtures through the API or the system context and describes the owner's call; the runner (apps/testing/contract/runner.ts) derives the checks from the registry: closed schemas (unknown body member -> 422 UNKNOWN_FIELD, unknown query parameter -> 400 UNKNOWN_QUERY_PARAM), the success response checked by the pipeline (status, closed response schema, AUD audit entry, PII read-audit for staff), admin-plane mechanics (PURP without/with a foreign purpose -> 400/404, RSN DELETE without CarPal-Reason -> 422, 4EYES -> 202 PendingChange pending, then rejected by a second admin), same-organization BFLA (colleagues with every role outside the sec line send the owner's exact request -> 404), BOLA (another user, or the same role in another organization with its own path -> 404 NOT_FOUND / 422 REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND, never data; body references for SEC-AZ-4), the kill switch (every FLAG(ai.*) route -> 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE on a kill-switch host, and every other owner call of the sweep runs on that host and succeeds) and the SEC-OUT-1/2 projection scan (forbidden fields, password hashes, full VINs of the sweep, trade prices outside the vendor's members or an approved trade account). The guard-level BFLA matrix of every route stays in routes.int.test.ts. A unit test checks that the suites are fresh, that every route has a resolver and that no response schema of the registry can carry a SEC-OUT-1 field, a full VIN (only vehicles.vin_reveal) or price_trade outside the vendor's own inventory routes. Findings: published organizations had no slug, so public.org_get could not reach them (fixed: the first publish assigns a default slug); VinDecodeResult.suggested admitted vin (contract tightened). Everything else held: 457 owner calls, 716 schema negatives, 224 BOLA checks, 200 same-organization BFLA checks, 30 admin-plane checks and 16 kill-switch checks pass.

ops_deferred.reason: Post-MVP (OQ-06, PM-01): the sweep asserts its 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED (answered before input validation, GD-05).
The signed storage PUT (host storage) is not an API route: the generated suite does not list it; media.int.test.ts covers it. S9c teaches contract:coverage the storage route.

report.tests: 992 passing (85 files) (pnpm test:all): S9b added 474 integration tests (17 suites: 457 routes + one registry/resolver check per module) and 7 unit tests (6 sweep checks: suites fresh, every route has a resolver, no SEC-OUT-1 field / full VIN / trade price reachable in any response schema, the dynamic scan itself; 1 defaultSlug rule). Sweep figures (pnpm vitest run apps/testing/contract --reporter=verbose prints one line per module): 457 owner calls, 716 schema negatives, 200 same-organization BFLA checks, 224 BOLA checks (236 not applicable: public, staff-plane, collection routes), 30 admin-plane checks, 16 kill-switch checks; about 3.5 minutes. Also green: pnpm lint (489 modules), typecheck, build, format:check, contract:check (incl. contract:tests --check), db:codegen --verify; contract:coverage 404/406 (unchanged).
deviations: GD-36: contract sweep = generated per-module suites (route lists from operations.json) + hand-written per-operation resolvers; request bodies are written per operation (copied from the module tests) rather than synthesized from the schemas, because valid requests need linked records (taxonomy chains, media of the right purpose, consents, plans).

Defect fixed (found by the sweep): org.create never sets a slug and nothing else did, so a published organization had no public profile URL (public.org_get resolves by slug only). activateOrganization (provider.publish, vendor.publish) now assigns defaultSlug(name, id) when the slug is null: Latin letters/digits of the name + the last 12 hex digits of the id ("org-<hex>" for non-Latin names); owners change it with org.update.

Contract hardening (DI-70): Docs/40 VinDecodeResult.suggested is Partial<Omit<VehicleWrite,'vin'>> instead of Partial<VehicleWrite>, so the closed response schema enforces SEC-OUT-2 (the lite decoder never suggested a VIN; the sweep checks it).

The sweep's api host runs with the AI kill switch on for every non-AI operation (and the Should-have flags community.comments/feed and qna on): graceful degradation is proven for the whole non-AI surface, not only search, profiles and appointments.

BOLA expectations that are not 404/422, by design: search.page -> 400 CURSOR_MISMATCH (the required cursor is signed for its caller and session, refused before the session is read); provider.service_record_create with another customer's vehicle -> 403 CONSENT_REQUIRED (unknown vehicles fail closed like a missing consent); LNK operations (org.invitation_accept, review_invitations.verify, consents.request_view/respond) -> 403 LINK_RECIPIENT_MISMATCH for another signed-in user.

Accepted as designed (no data, no existence oracle): notifications.mark_read ignores ids outside the caller's notifications (RLS; checked in the resolver that they stay unread) and inventory.bulk_update skips items outside the vendor; public-by-design references (follows/favorites of published organizations, transfer requests by VIN, trade account and partner requests naming published organizations) have no BOLA check.

Entitlement (ENT) and consent (CNS) gates run before body-reference checks, so the cross-tenant attackers of inventory.import_create, fleet.import_create, ai.inventory_normalize and ai.fleet_suggestions are organizations on the same plan with the same consent.

Purpose binding (SEC-ADM-5) is checked per queue item in the caller's queue (as the contract words it), not per record: a purpose of an open case about user A also unlocks user B. Kept for the next iteration (hardening list of S8).
ai.profile_helper needs an existing provider profile (404 otherwise); the sweep calls it on a published provider.

Sweep fixtures that the shared test database must not keep (seeded taxonomy counts, MCP clients) are removed when a suite ends (Harness.onClose); four-eyes requests are rejected by a second admin and stale pending changes of fixed targets (plans, retention policies) are expired first.
notes_for_next: S9c OpenAPI: describe the regenerated VinDecodeResult (DI-70); the resolvers in apps/testing/contract/resolvers are a source of valid request examples per operation.

S9c CI: run pnpm lint, typecheck, build, format:check, contract:check (now including the sweep-suite freshness check), db:codegen --verify and pnpm test:all (about 8 minutes; integration project single worker on embedded PostgreSQL).
S9c README: document pnpm contract:tests and the rule that every new operation needs a resolver (the generated suite fails otherwise); point to the per-module stats line of the verbose reporter.

Appendix C items outside the sweep stay where they are: C.5 security mechanics (DPoP, refresh-family reuse, IDEM replay/conflict, ETAG, single-use links, step-up, timings, map-link SSRF) in pipeline/auth-server/organization tests; C.6 rate limits and load shedding in the pipeline tests; C.7 business rules in the module tests.
Next iteration: purpose binding to the record being read (SEC-ADM-5 hardening); a generic READ_ONLY_FIELD probe per input schema (S fields), which needs the S-field list from 52 in the generator.

tasks.title: search.session_get and search.page limit (pwa DI-46, backend DI-46). GET /v1/search/{session_id}?limit returns the stored first page as a SearchResponse: the chips of the stored intent, the safety block, vehicle_filter_fallback and the facets as computed at run time. Store the SafetyBlock, the fallback flag and the facets with the session, either in the StoredIntent JSON of interpreted_intent or as new MatchSession S fields with a numbered 43 migration and 52 entries; record the choice. Cards come from the stored results through resultCards with current public data; results that are no longer public are skipped as in search.page. Return a fresh next_cursor. Answer 404 for another caller's session (RLS requester_all) and for sessions created more than 24 hours ago. No analytics event and no new MatchSession. search.page honours limit (Int<1,50>, default 20); the cursor keeps carrying the offset.

tasks.title: Facets (pwa DI-42). With SearchRequest.facets (refine defaults to the refined session's value), rank() retrieves the base set once without the facetable filters, i.e. the SearchFilters members named in FacetKey. It evaluates each of those filters per candidate in memory, using the same predicates as today's index filters and in-memory filters (open_now, available_within_days, stock_available), and keeps as results the candidates that pass every active filter; they must equal the run without facets. Counts: for each option, the candidates that pass every active filter except the facet's own, plus this option (options of a Set facet combine with OR). Value encoding: booleans 'true'; min_rating '3', '3.5', '4', '4.5' (rating ≥ value); available_within_days '0' and '7'; node facets list the selected nodes plus the 20 nodes with the most results (service systems from the provider docs, part categories from the vendor and item docs). without_filter has one entry per active facetable filter. result_count is counted before the 100-result cap. capped is true when any retrieval returned its size limit (500 providers, 500 vendors, 1000 items). The vehicle filter and its fallback apply to every count as in the run. Facets cover only the keys that apply to the target type: provider facets for provider, vendor and item facets for vendor and inventory_item, both for place. Store the facets with the session (T2). Without facets, retrieval stays as it is today.
tasks.result: done: modules/discovery/domain/facets.ts (pure: facet keys per target, options, the document filters PROVIDER_FILTERS / VENDOR_FILTERS / ITEM_FILTERS shared by retrieval, facets and the map, computeFacets). SearchService.rank was split into #collect (retrieval + scores) and #select (membership of one filter set: index filters via matchesFilter, the text retry, availability, hybrid merge, open now, vehicle fallback). A run uses #collect without facets exactly as before; SearchRequest.facets adds a second #collect without the facetable filters (size 1000) and counts each option with #select, so a count is by construction the result count of a run with that option. Stored with the session.

Fill ResultCard.next_available_slot with the provider's earliest open slot in the next 30 days, the same calculation as public.availability (AppointmentRead.nextOpenSlot). Take it from the projection, and never return a passed slot: for the page's providers, re-read a passed value through nextOpenSlot, or return null. Add a W15 scheduled rule (41 §6.3) that re-projects providers whose next_available_at has passed, at least every 15 minutes. SearchSort 'soonest' in run and refine: providers with a slot ascending by slot, ties by score; then providers without a slot, vendors and items in best-match order; inactive providers last (54 §6). The safety-critical urgent-first rule stays limited to best_match, as today; record it if that changes. The sort is stored in StoredIntent.sort, so refine and session_get keep it.

Pipeline order: closed-schema validation (query and body) runs after authorization and the 501 check, not in transport step 3 of 41 §5; parsing limits stay in step 3. Rate limiting is split: caller windows before authorization, organization windows after it.
GD-05: 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED is answered after authentication, authorization and flags (so the sweep proves every route's guards), with a Problem code outside the 40 catalog (dev only).
CarPal-Client is not required on token-less GET routes (discovery documents, /oauth/authorize navigation, health.get); 40 §1.3 says 'Always'.
jobs.cancel: only the job's owner may cancel (description 'the caller started'), although sec is USR | ORG(ANY); org members who are not the owner get 404.
PURP: a missing or malformed CarPal-Access-Purpose is 400 MALFORMED_REQUEST (40 names no code); binding to the staff queue is a stub that accepts well-formed purposes until S8.
DriverAssignments is a deny-all stub until fleet (S8): fleet drivers get 404 on {flt}/vehicles/{vehicle_id} routes.

MembershipDirectory and OrganizationDirectory are provisional DB-backed implementations in modules/identity and modules/organization (instead of in-memory stubs), so fixtures and RLS agree; S3/S4 extend them.
Lite rate limits, sessions, idempotency and the event bus are per process: separate deployables need full mode (Redis/NATS); pnpm dev runs everything in one process.
Node >= 24.7 required (crypto.argon2) instead of >= 22.12 (GD-10 amendment).
Docs/43 fixed in place (publish_event, write_audit SECURITY DEFINER) per database/migrations/README.md (no shared environment yet); local DBs need pnpm db:reset.

Deferred (501): auth.webauthn_options, me.webauthn_register_options, auth.social_start (OQ-04, OQ-06). Consequently staff cannot sign in through the hosted UI (cp-web-admin needs aal3 WebAuthn); admin-plane tests keep using fixture sessions.
AAL2 for accounts without a second factor: a sign-in within the 10-minute window satisfies it (Session.mfaEnrolled = false), DI-11.

Strict-mode gaps (GD-06): App Attest / Play Integrity tokens are refused (PoW only); private_key_jwt / mTLS client authentication of cp-web-* and cp-ssr is not enforced at /oauth/token (client_id is trusted); DPoP-Nonce is required only at the token endpoint, not on the API hosts.
SEC-AU-12 risk-based sign-in (new-device notices, exponential slow-down per account and IP, impossible travel) is not implemented; the auth.signin / auth.otp rate-limit buckets apply.
Breached-password check uses a small built-in list and trivial patterns (no breached corpus in lite mode, OQ-05); refusal is VALIDATION_FAILED with field code "pattern" (DI-13).
Session country is not resolved (null); the device label comes from CarPal-Client.
Hosted sign-in completion re-requests /oauth/authorize (cookie-bound interaction); interaction errors are 410 LINK_EXPIRED (DI-15).
onboarding.update creates a missing flow on If-Match "v1" (DI-14).
auth.email_verify answers 409 DUPLICATE when an email change targets an address taken meanwhile (DI-16).

Identity mails and texts go straight to the Mailer/SmsSender ports with template keys (identity.*); the refresh-token reuse alert is an email, not yet a system_announcement notification (S6 notification module).
SMS to a country code outside the region allowlist is 422 VALIDATION_FAILED (pointer /phone or /destination, code enum); 40 names no code.
consents.grant fails closed for scope types whose owning module has not registered a ConsentScopes verifier yet (all five until S4/S5/S7) and for mcp_client grantees (until S8/S9).

dsr.export_download answers 410 for completed exports until media binds DataExportFiles (S4/S8); subscription.org_get answers 404 for organizations without a subscription (org.create creates one in S4).
Taxonomy version is derived from the data fingerprint instead of the catalog version "1.0.0"; config.client reports the same value.
libs/safety-check Urgency renamed critical → safety_critical to match 52 / core.urgency_level.
Docs/43 changed in place (three definer functions, DI-17); local databases need pnpm db:reset.
Contract generator fixes changed operation-schemas.json for 26 GET list operations (cursor/limit) and 6 path parameters (DI-12).

Lite storage serves signed URLs over http (local listener) while 40 Url is https-only: the response check rewrites those URLs to an https placeholder in lite mode only; clients receive them unchanged (full mode unaffected).

W6 lite: no real malware scanner (the EICAR test signature stands in), videos are not transcoded (exif_stripped stays false, so videos are never publicly servable in lite mode), PDFs are not sanitized; HEIC (HEVC) cannot be decoded by prebuilt sharp, so HEIC uploads end scan_status failed / quarantined.
Raw uploads are plaintext in storage until W6 re-stores them (encrypted when private or a document); the lite listener's PUT has no encryption.

Lite geocoder = FixtureGeocoder (a few pilot-city street addresses + city centres); unknown addresses give location_check_status not_checked. Full mode answers 503 until the regional geocoder adapter exists.
Slug changes (≤ 2 per 30 days) are counted in the KV store (no column); lite KV is per process, so the count resets on restart. Over the limit: 429 RATE_LIMITED (40 names no code).

Portfolio publication stops at pending_review: moderation approval, published_at and portfolio.published belong to the S8 moderation queue. Asset moderation_status also stays pending, so no media is publicly servable before S8.

Visits, customers, vehicle owners and inventory counts come from OrganizationExtensions; until S5/S7 register resolvers, linked appointments/service records and customer notes answer 422 REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND and job-log vehicle links 403 CONSENT_REQUIRED (fail closed).

provider.insights_get / vendor.insights_get return completeness, response time and catalog score from this module and 0/null for figures of other modules (reviews, requests, views, inquiries) until they register insight sources; the plan's '503 AI_UNAVAILABLE until S9' did not apply (the operations carry no FLAG and are not AI).
ai_approved portfolio captions and apply_suggestions redaction need AI insights (S9): until then 422 at /ai_caption_insight_id and /decision.

provider.coverage_create / vendor.coverage_create: an unknown node or wrong node type anywhere fails the whole request through the pipeline's NodeId check (GD-17); parent-chain and duplicate problems are skipped per row (codes reference_not_found, conditional_required, not_unique; vendor type mismatch: enum).
org.members_list never lists removed memberships (their user data is invisible under RLS); status=removed returns an empty page.

First active location becomes primary even if is_primary=false was sent (52: exactly one primary); org.location_create/update with a second primary: 422 VALIDATION_FAILED /is_primary not_unique (primary_conflict).
org.member_remove by a manager on an equal or higher role: 404 (authorization qualifier, SEC-AZ-2); member_invite role not allowed: 422 /role enum.
media.get for a pending_upload asset is 404 (MediaAsset.status has no pending_upload, DI-25); upload_complete for an already completed asset returns its current state.
Hybrid organizations: the creator is provider_owner and cannot use {vnd} routes (V+/V* need vendor roles) until DI-21 is decided; an owner may invite a separate vendor_owner.
Media attach: logo, avatar and cover replace the previous active attachment of the same role on the record.
Docs/40, Docs/42 and Docs/43 changed in place (Problem members, OrgMember, consent_request_contact, accept_invitation); local databases need pnpm db:reset.
Fleet drivers reach no vehicle until S8 binds DriverAssignments (fail closed): driver lists are empty and every path-vehicle route is 404; Vehicle.assigned_driver is always null.
VIN decoder: lite decodes only the model year (position 10, suggestions only, decode_status partial or failed); full mode answers 503 UNAVAILABLE(decoder) until a regional adapter exists (OQ-10).

provider.service_record_create through appointment_id answers 422 REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND until S7; provider records and job-log links for fleet vehicles answer 403 CONSENT_REQUIRED (DI-38). Fleet documents are shared with a provider by role, without a consent record (DI-38).
invoice_upload records stay self_reported: the invoice verification path (staff or AI) belongs to S8/S9.

Driver issue reports set fleet_approval_status pending and publish fleet.approval.requested; the FleetApproval record itself is created by the fleet module (S8, from the event or fleet.approval_create).

Notifications are events only (vehicle.reminder.due, inquiry.sent …); delivery and templates come with S6. vehicle.reminder.due is not in 40 Appendix A yet (DI-36). Rule reminders are titled in English ("Renew <document title>").

CSV imports: categories by taxonomy node id only (no slug or label matching, DI-41); ai_normalization_requested is recorded for S9; the whole file is read into memory (≤ 20 MB, SEC-IN-11); the error report object is written before its asset row (a rolled-back transaction leaves an unreferenced object for the S8 retention purge).
inventory.search is a parameterized substring match over SKU, part numbers and names (no ranking); public search ranking belongs to S6.
Item data quality depends on image attachments, which change in the media module without an event: scores refresh on item writes, after imports and by the daily rule (DI-43).

Catalog quality and measured response time are written to the vendor profile when they change, which moves its version (a client holding an older ETag gets 412 VERSION_MISMATCH on vendor.profile_put and re-reads).
StockInquiry.can_review is true for the requester of a completed inquiry; whether a review already exists is checked by the trust module (S7).
reminders.delete soft-deletes (deleted_at); vehicle documents, service records and evidence are status removed and stay for audit.
Docs/43 and Docs/42 changed in place again (definer functions, inquiry trigger, jobs rule): local databases need pnpm db:reset.
public.availability is a placeholder: it checks the published provider and the location and answers { slots: [] } until S7 computes slots (DI-53).
public.org_reviews lives in a new trust module with only its read side (TrustRead); reviews exist only once S7 writes them (tests insert fixture rows).

Community text is pre-moderated automatically (GD-22, OQ-12): links, emails and phone numbers wait for the S8 queue; media stay private until S8 approves them, so public posts, questions and showcases show no media yet; author avatars are always null.

Search: search_mode showcases/qna rank providers (DI-48); issue_id is ignored (DI-49); available_within_days is ignored and preferred_partners_only fails closed (DI-53); trust scores, availability and freshness are not ranking inputs until S7 (category trust uses published ratings, operational fit the response time); the default search radius is 50 km (proposed).
Lite search index is per process (like the other lite adapters): separate deployables need the OpenSearch adapter, which is written but unverified (OQ-01).
Edits of service categories, coverage, capabilities, certifications and portfolio reach the index through the one-minute sweep, not an event (DI-45).
search.page pages hold 20 results (no limit in the contract, DI-46); questions send their ETag in a header (DI-47).

Reactions on a target bump its version when the cached counter changes (posts, answers): an author holding an older ETag gets 412 and re-reads; portfolio like_count follows asynchronously (community.reaction.changed).
Deleting an accepted answer is 409 INVALID_TRANSITION (DI-51); a push token already registered by another account is 409 DUPLICATE (DI-52).

Notifications: no notification for new questions, answers or service records yet (no recipient rule in 52 for them); SMS only when the user enables it and has a verified phone; push sending in full mode needs the push gateway adapter (skeleton).

The identity mails keep being sent synchronously by the auth server (now through the Messenger with EN/FA templates); the refresh-token reuse alert is additionally a critical in-app system_announcement via user.security_alert, written in its own transaction because the token request rolls back.
Anonymous principals' anonKey is now the full 64-hex HMAC (was 32) to satisfy discovery.match_sessions.anonymous_key_hash.
Docs/43 and Docs/42 changed in place again (community.refresh_reaction_count): local databases need pnpm db:reset.

Docs/43 and Docs/42 §5.3 changed in place again: definers appointment.requester_contact, appointment.check_in_contact, appointment.visit_cards, appointment.busy_intervals, trust.invitation_contact, trust.invitation_by_token, trust.claim_invitation, media.shared_attachments; appointment.capacity_available is now SECURITY DEFINER (a requester accepting an alternative must count every party's appointments). Local databases need pnpm db:reset.
A location without any active availability rule has no calendar: confirmation checks only time off (under the same advisory lock) and public.availability offers no slots there (DI-56).

Path 2 reviews are never published in S7: the business answer, the 7-day no_response rule and the objection dispute exist, but the CarPal reviewer decision is an admin operation (§23.4, S8). The database check reviews_path2_publish_rule is covered by a test.

W4 automatic checks are text rules only: links, email addresses and phone numbers hold a Path 1 review in pending_moderation for the S8 queue (same rule as GD-22); the SEC-BF-1 fraud signals (device-key hash, IP prefix, timing) and the SEC-BF-2 same-device/same-network invitation checks have no data source yet; members of the subject are refused.

Fleets: share_history is ignored for fleet requests (no personal consent subject, DI-38/DI-58); fleet_approval_id is refused (fleet approvals arrive in S8); fleet appointments get no system review invitation (fleet_confirmed needs the fleet workflow); a cost estimate above a fleet threshold publishes nothing yet; fleet drivers (F*) see only appointments they requested until S8 binds assignments (GD-20).

AI: triage_session_id is refused (Help Me sessions, S9); the pre-visit ai_summary stays null (ai_summary_status not_required); review response drafts from AI insights are refused (ai_draft_insight_id → 422).

Events beyond 40 Appendix A (DI-54): appointment.reminder.due, appointment.note_added, appointment.delay_reported, appointment.availability.changed, review.edited, review.removed, review.response.published, review.response.removed, review.invitation.reminded, dispute.opened, inquiry.status_changed.
Disputes about service records and moderation actions are refused (REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND) until the S8 queues exist; badge challenges are open to any signed-in user.
Appointment.requester_contact is the verified email or phone of the preferred channel only; it is null when the preference is in_app or push (DI-57).

The ci check-in link is mailed by the Messenger at confirmation (it carries a token, GD-24); the appointment.confirmed notification is in-app and push only. Check-in by link needs an anonymous token like the other PUB link operations.

trust.score.changed is published on every score change (the W2 indexer needs it), the audit entry only for changes above 5 points or the first score (54 §9.4, DI-60); trust signals get a new row only when a value changes.

Review evidence base weights are stored rounded (smallint): a Path 2 five-star review counts 5, not 4.8 (DI-61). Evidence without a matching capability creates a system-level capability (source job_evidence/review_evidence/certification, not public).
review_responses.update keeps a published response published (responses have no moderation status yet, DI-59).

A user may write one review without a visit per subject (eligibility already_reviewed); proposed velocity limit 5 reviews per author per 24 h (REVIEW_NOT_ALLOWED); SEC-BF-3 caps 3 open requests per provider and 10 in total plus a 7-day cooldown after a no-show answer 429 RATE_LIMITED (DI-55).
An appointment created from an issue schedules the issue when the request is sent (requester context), not at confirmation: the provider cannot read the customer's issues.
The completion service record drops inventory references from parts (the provider names its parts) and is written only when a service system is known (body or appointment).
The plan's KV slot cache was not built: slots are computed per request from the rules, time off and the busy_intervals definer.

Docs/40 changed (contract regenerated): FeatureFlag and McpClientView gained version (their update operations are ETAG; clients could not send If-Match), TaxonomyNode gained an optional version (staff responses only), §1.3 gained the CarPal-Reason header (DI-09 decided). Docs/43 + 42 §5.3 gained the definer admin.moderation_action_affects: run `pnpm db:reset` once.
DI-09 decided: RSN on DELETE (admin.platform_role_revoke, admin.synonym_delete) reads the reason from the CarPal-Reason header (422 VALIDATION_FAILED at /reason when missing).

Purpose binding (SEC-ADM-5): case and dispute purposes must be unassigned or assigned to the caller; DSR, verification and approval items form shared open queues (any staff member with the operation's role may act on an open item). A purpose is not checked against the record being read (a case about user A can be used to read user B); S9 hardening may bind them.

Four-eyes: one pending change per operation and target (409 DUPLICATE for a second); executors run in the approver's transaction with the approver as actor, the audit entry names the original requester. admin.mcp_client_update reactivation also needs a second admin (only suspension and revocation are immediate).

Assisted onboarding: sessions are recorded (≤ 4 h, one active per organization, assist_onboarding action) but the {adm}/assist/{session}/… routes are not served (not in the registry): DI-05 stays open.

case_action: actions owned by dedicated operations (verify_organization, reject_verification, confirm/reject_review_approval, request_evidence, correct_location, assist_onboarding) answer 409 INVALID_TRANSITION; merge_duplicate files an admin.org_merge four-eyes change; warn_user only records and notifies.
admin.user_status suspend_until is recorded on the moderation action but suspensions are not lifted automatically (no rule yet).
admin.org_merge marks the duplicate merged and unpublishes its profiles; memberships, locations, reviews and other references are not re-pointed (they resolve through merged_into_organization_id).

Taxonomy merge re-points simple node columns in vehicle, appointment, trust (reviews), organization (portfolio items), inventory (item categories), fleet (partners) and taxonomy itself; rows with unique keys (capabilities, coverage, service categories, review tags, synonym/mapping duplicates) keep the merged id and resolve through canonicalId.

Events outside 40 Appendix A: feature_flag.changed (cache bust), user.deletion.requested (approved deletion → worker), dsr.deadline.approaching (staff alert), review.removed/review.response.removed from moderation; fleet.approval.requested is also published by provider.appointments_update WITHOUT an approval (the fleet consumer decides; W5 notifies only events with approval_id).

Notifications: fleet.approval.decided uses event_type system_announcement (52 Notification.event_type has no decision type); moderation outcomes, verification and location corrections use moderation_update; DSR alerts moderation_alert to platform admins and support.

DSR export bundle is CSV in long format (section, record_id, field, value): media mime types allow PDF/CSV only, not JSON. Erasure: identity anonymizes the account (email deleted-<id>@deleted.carpal.invalid, status deleted) and deletes credentials, tokens, onboarding; consents withdrawn; memberships removed; vehicles soft-deleted with VIN/plate cleared; media removed; notifications, preferences, push tokens deleted; match sessions anonymized; provider notes about the user deleted; driver assignments ended; appointment descriptions replaced; unpublished reviews removed (published reviews stay under 'former member'); inquiry vehicle snapshots cleared; pseudonym key deleted. AI records (triage sessions, insights) are not erased yet (S9).

Analytics: dashboards ignore the region and organization_type query filters (aggregates are stored without dimensions); retention of AnalyticsEvent (writer cannot delete), McpAccessLog (append-only) and AuditLog/Review/DSR archive policies are not applied; analytics never blocks the product (a failed ingest batch is logged and dropped).

Fleet: approval_workflow_enabled defaults to on without a profile (DB default); coordinators (and drivers) need an approved repair_request or provider_selection approval for fleet appointments while the workflow is on, owners and managers do not; drivers read appointments of their assigned vehicles (list/get) but only their own requests elsewhere; dashboard active_repairs = max(active fleet appointments, vehicles in_repair); reports compute per request (no materialized aggregates); exports keep files 7 days; FleetExport retention deletes rows (their private files stay unreachable). Fleet trust signals (54 §8) and fleet_friendly revocation are not computed yet.
A fleet search with preferred_partners_only returns preferred providers only (vendors and items are left out); the preferred bonus is +5, cumulative with a favourite up to +10.

Moderation intake opens system_rule cases (reason other, severity low) for held reviews (pending_moderation), community content (moderation pending), portfolio items (pending_review) and public media (moderation pending, except portfolio media which follow their item).

The API roles cannot use the system RLS context: driver assignment checks run in the driver's own context; report targets are checked in the reporter's context (definer cards for users and organizations).
WebAuthn (OQ-04) is still not implemented: staff aal3 sessions exist only through fixtures/tests; auth.webauthn_options, me.webauthn_register_options and auth.social_start stay deferred (S3).

GD-35: the MCP gateway runs in process (lite) with its own carpal_ai pool; McpClientPort = deterministic stub (dev default) or "unavailable" (staging/prod default until D6/D7 exist): every AI operation then answers 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE and the non-AI paths carry on.
triage.start / triage.reply check their own FLAG (ChecksOwnFlags) so the 503 carries the safety block; Problem gained safety, fallback_path and vin_transfer_available (Docs/40 §4.2).

Triage turns are validated but not stored as insights; the final triage_summary insight is created on completion (user-private: organization null, also for fleet vehicles). Fleet membership for triage on fleet vehicles is resolved through the vehicle.vehicle_fleet_owner definer; draft_appointment_with is personal sessions only; fleet viewers cannot create issues.

Approval requests are created for staff-level members' drafts of external actions only (publish_showcase by provider_staff, apply_inventory_normalization by vendor_staff); drafts by P+/V+ are approved by the domain publish operation (SEC-AI-3). ORG(by approver_role) admits the approver role or a higher role of the same organization type.

Suggestion appliers: vehicle (series/engine/fuel), maintenance_reminder (add, source ai_suggestion), inventory_item (normalized name, category). Profile-gap suggestions are informational (action review). Capability/coverage, fitment and redaction suggestions are pending domain records decided with provider.gated_decide / fitment.decide / media.redaction_decide.
ai.suggestions_list, ai.suggestions_mine and ai.approvals_list default to status pending when no status is given.

Context packages come from the owning modules through AiContextSources (registered readers over their own tables); search.part_demand reads aggregated match-session counts in the worker's system context (W9 only).

W9 event-driven insights are limited to imports that asked for AI normalization (vendor.inventory.imported); the other 41 §2.4 W9 events are not wired (the §21 operations are on demand, no unrequested AI output).

W10 classification uses the capability level when category rating and local demand are not available (>=3 strong; rising or level 2 emerging; <=1 weak; opportunity not assigned); rating_trend, repeat customers and local demand stay null.

W11 rules: repeated text (hash of normalized text, >= 2 reviews in 7 days) and five same-extreme ratings within 24 h; the new-account burst signal needs identity facts and is not computed. Cases: source ai_flag, reason fake, severity medium.
W14 is a skeleton (no embedding model in lite); semantic search, AI query interpretation and AI match explanations stay rule-based (next iteration).

DSR erase anonymizes personal insights (owner null, internal, "[erased]") because append-only evaluation records reference them; evaluation records keep actor ids and comments (append-only for every role).
A failed AI job ends with error_code AI_UNAVAILABLE (no retry).

The fleet_assistant MCP client got vehicle.extract_fields, vehicle.suggest_maintenance and vehicle.summarize_history (Docs/43 §22.5) for the fleet path of ai.vehicle_suggestions / ai.service_history_insights.

WebAuthn: a pending authentication method holds the registration challenge; clients take its id from me.mfa_list (me.webauthn_register_options returns standard creation options only). Passkey sign-in = auth.webauthn_options purpose signin + auth.mfa_verify method webauthn without a first factor. Device-bound credentials (no backup flags) give aal3, synced passkeys aal2; the admin client accepts device-bound keys only. RP ID carpal.app, origins from CARPAL_WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS; algorithms EdDSA/ES256/RS256.
Media (GD-32): image/heic left the accepted upload types (422 at media.upload_init); MAX_VIDEO_SECONDS 15.

VIN (GD-33): global unique index vehicles_vin_uq; Vehicle.duplicate_vin_warning stays in the contract but is always false. Transfers: 4 new operations and the {VT} path alias (contract 406 ops / 458 routes); acceptance through vehicle.accept_transfer; vehicle.transferred moves media ownership, ends fleet driver assignments and withdraws the previous owner's vehicle-scoped consents.

Fleet sharing (GD-34): Vehicle.data_sharing (fleet owners/managers); appointments.consent_to_share_history may be true without a consent record for fleet requests (Docs/43 constraint relaxed); PreVisitReport.shared_documents with 5-minute URLs; providers check the vehicle's sharing live; fleet.vehicle_data.shared notifies fleet owners and managers. Fleet approvals do not copy ai_triage_insight_id.
SearchService.run was split into runIn (Help Me matches in the caller's transaction); Help Me match sessions store issue_id and triage_session_id.
The coverage tool reads every id of a multi-id @Operation(...) decorator.

GD-36: contract sweep = generated per-module suites (route lists from operations.json) + hand-written per-operation resolvers; request bodies are written per operation (copied from the module tests) rather than synthesized from the schemas, because valid requests need linked records (taxonomy chains, media of the right purpose, consents, plans).

Defect fixed (found by the sweep): org.create never sets a slug and nothing else did, so a published organization had no public profile URL (public.org_get resolves by slug only). activateOrganization (provider.publish, vendor.publish) now assigns defaultSlug(name, id) when the slug is null: Latin letters/digits of the name + the last 12 hex digits of the id ("org-<hex>" for non-Latin names); owners change it with org.update.

Contract hardening (DI-70): Docs/40 VinDecodeResult.suggested is Partial<Omit<VehicleWrite,'vin'>> instead of Partial<VehicleWrite>, so the closed response schema enforces SEC-OUT-2 (the lite decoder never suggested a VIN; the sweep checks it).

The sweep's api host runs with the AI kill switch on for every non-AI operation (and the Should-have flags community.comments/feed and qna on): graceful degradation is proven for the whole non-AI surface, not only search, profiles and appointments.

BOLA expectations that are not 404/422, by design: search.page -> 400 CURSOR_MISMATCH (the required cursor is signed for its caller and session, refused before the session is read); provider.service_record_create with another customer's vehicle -> 403 CONSENT_REQUIRED (unknown vehicles fail closed like a missing consent); LNK operations (org.invitation_accept, review_invitations.verify, consents.request_view/respond) -> 403 LINK_RECIPIENT_MISMATCH for another signed-in user.

Accepted as designed (no data, no existence oracle): notifications.mark_read ignores ids outside the caller's notifications (RLS; checked in the resolver that they stay unread) and inventory.bulk_update skips items outside the vendor; public-by-design references (follows/favorites of published organizations, transfer requests by VIN, trade account and partner requests naming published organizations) have no BOLA check.

Entitlement (ENT) and consent (CNS) gates run before body-reference checks, so the cross-tenant attackers of inventory.import_create, fleet.import_create, ai.inventory_normalize and ai.fleet_suggestions are organizations on the same plan with the same consent.

Purpose binding (SEC-ADM-5) is checked per queue item in the caller's queue (as the contract words it), not per record: a purpose of an open case about user A also unlocks user B. Kept for the next iteration (hardening list of S8).
ai.profile_helper needs an existing provider profile (404 otherwise); the sweep calls it on a published provider.

Sweep fixtures that the shared test database must not keep (seeded taxonomy counts, MCP clients) are removed when a suite ends (Harness.onClose); four-eyes requests are rejected by a second admin and stale pending changes of fixed targets (plans, retention policies) are expired first.

GD-37: OpenAPI is generated from the contract registry and schemas (tools/contract/openapi.ts), not from NestJS decorators (there are no controllers, GD-12); 40 "generated from NestJS" is read as "generated from the backend that serves it" and the equivalence is enforced by pnpm openapi:check against the registry and every host router.

GD-38: fleet drivers are narrowed below ORG(ANY) on fleet records reached by id (WP0 narrowing, 40 §0.5): fleet media only when uploaded by them or attached to an assigned vehicle record (changes: own uploads only); fleet AI insights and suggestions never (404).
DI-71: vehicles.status_history, appointments.history and appointments.notes_list got DRV in Docs/40 (the appointment reads were already filtered by the handler); SEC-AZ-7 text extended.

DI-50 resolved: the server-defined Json<...> schemas are written down as OpenAPI components; open-ended ones (MatchReasonValues, FeedCard, TemplateParams, BadgeEvaluation, TargetSnapshot) are described as constrained maps with their known keys rather than closed objects.
The storage PUT is documented as PUT /o/{object_key} on the media host with x-carpal-path-template <UploadTicket.url>: clients must use the ticket URL as given.
The YAML is written by a small in-repo emitter (tools/contract/yaml.ts) because S9c adds no npm dependency; strings are plain only when unambiguous, otherwise JSON-quoted.
S9b note corrected: routes.int.test.ts tried only the first allowed role from a foreign organization (not every role); it now tries every allowed role.
The fleet-driver sweep check runs on {flt} vehicle and appointment routes whose sec line admits drivers; on lists it requires 200 with none of the owner records (driver without an assignment).
Media attached to non-vehicle fleet records (appointments, stock inquiries) reaches a driver only through their own uploads (RCP-02 gap).

ProtocolError lists the RFC 6749 codes the auth server emits (invalid_grant, invalid_dpop_proof, use_dpop_nonce, invalid_client, invalid_request, invalid_scope, unauthorized_client, unsupported_grant_type) although 40 names only four.
Link-token refusals (LINK_RECIPIENT_MISMATCH vs LINK_EXPIRED) are distinguishable by the token holder by contract; accepted as RCP-04 (pending product confirmation).
ClientConfig.contract_version widened from the literal '1.0.0' to Str<5,20> (DI-74): the field reports the header's version; the PWA's generated types will see a string.

Contract 1.1.0 corrected before use (DI-74): service_system_node_ids and part_category_node_ids are not facets (in search they widen the request together with the chips: a count 'with this option' would not narrow); facets are listed per target type; languages lists the selected ones plus the 20 spoken by the most results (Lang is an open ISO code).

available_within_days: 0 was ignored (a falsy check) although the PWA sends it for 'Today'; now it filters (before the end of today in the location's time zone). N > 14 also changes: the projection now looks 30 days ahead, so providers with a first slot between day 15 and 30 pass larger windows.
Session response state (safety block, fallback, facets, facets flag) is stored in interpreted_intent (StoredIntent) instead of new MatchSession columns: no migration; Docs/52 says so.

A passed projected slot is re-read in the caller's transaction (the api role may not use the system context: 'role carpal_api may not use the system context'); ranking still uses the projected value until the W15 rule refreshes it (at most 15 minutes).

Facets cost a second retrieval (providers/vendors at size 1000) and, for text queries, the text-free retry query; counts are evaluated in memory (about 60 selections over the pool for a provider search).
map.pins no longer runs a second filtered index query per layer: the same filters are judged on the viewport hits with matchesFilter (the index port's semantics).

The consumer BFF now exists in pwa/src/server/bff/ (framework-free, Request/Response only; NI-08 should reuse or move it rather than write a second one). Findings for the backend owner (pwa/dev_plan.json DI-24..DI-26): (1) Url is https-only, so a local browser sign-in needs the PWA on https (redirect_uri http://localhost is 422 pattern); (2) auth.token and /v1/auth/* are RL(auth.signin) with a 30 per 15 min per-IP-prefix window, and the pipeline takes the IP from the socket only, so every refresh, anonymous grant and hosted-UI sign-in that passes through the BFF counts against the BFF host's single IP — production needs a trusted forwarded client IP for the BFF (or exempting confidential-client token requests from the IP window); (3) token scopes are not enforced per operation (cp-ssr can call search.run), and a cp-ssr token is one anonymous principal (anonKey = HMAC(sub cp-ssr)), so all server rendering shares one public.read bucket (120/min, 3000/day) — cp-ssr needs its own bucket before P5/P6 SEO pages go live.

No backend code changed. Repository change outside pwa/: shared/region-config/package.json (private package @carpal/region-config exporting ./ir-pilot.json) so the PWA can bundle the pilot region file as its offline fallback for config.client; backend/libs/region-config still reads shared/region-config/<region_key>.json by path, unaffected. Findings for the backend owner (pwa/dev_plan.json DI-27..DI-29): (1) taxonomy.suggest is RL(search) — the guest search bucket (10/min anon) — so header typeahead competes with real searches; the PWA debounces 350 ms, caches per text and pauses after a 429, but a separate typeahead bucket (or suggest outside RL search) would serve guests better; (2) there is no primary/active vehicle field on Vehicle or the user profile, so the vehicle context chip is a per-browser choice in the PWA; a preference field would sync it across devices; (3) RegionConfig has no display currency unit (IRR shown as toman ÷ 10) and no time zone (the PWA defaults to Asia/Tehran until the browser's zone is known) — both belong in the region config if the product confirms them.

No backend code changed; backend/.env.example's PWA comment now also lists https://localhost:3100/bff/oauth/callback (the PWA's Playwright port). The hosted sign-in UI exists (pwa/src/app/id/signin, src/features/auth) and was run against this backend live. Findings for the backend owner (pwa/dev_plan.json DI-29..DI-36, OQ-17): (1) auth.authorize resumes a completed interaction only when prompt is not 'login', so the hosted UI re-requests the authorize URL without prompt; acr_values is stored on the interaction but not enforced — please confirm this resume contract (and consider enforcing acr_values or documenting the BA-11 recency rule there); (2) config.client has no Terms/Privacy policy versions and auth.signup takes no optional consents (marketing, AI personalisation), so the PWA uses env versions and grants those consents after the first sign-in — a policy-version field in config.client and optional consents on auth.signup would remove that; (3) no feed-preference operation for onboarding interests (topics, brands; follows.put takes organisations only); (4) vehicles.vin_decode needs a saved vehicle — a pre-save decode (e.g. vehicles.vin_decode_preview {vin}) would allow the C-ONB-01 'decode on paste' card; (5) suspended accounts get INVALID_CREDENTIALS like a wrong password, so S-AUTH-09 (reason, appeal, data export) cannot be shown — decide whether a correct credential may learn the state (OQ-17 in the PWA plan); (6) product decision OQ-11: prices are based in USD (with a per-browser conversion in the PWA), while shared/region-config/ir-pilot.json still says currency IRR — decide whether stored amounts move to USD; (7) the BFF can create two pre-sessions for one browser when two first requests race (fixed on the PWA's client side); when NI-08 moves the BFF, a server-side remedy is worth having.
